objects.description: No structs, enums, typedefs, or classes are defined in this header. It only declares two functions and two macros for version information.
No structs, enums, typedefs, or classes are defined in this header. It only provides byte-order (endian) read/write and bit-rotation macros. Consequently, there are no custom data types to document.
No custom data types (structs, enums, typedefs, or classes) are defined in this header. It only contains macros, function declarations, and includes.

objects.definition: typedef uint8_t hash256_t[32];
objects.description: A fixed-size 256-bit (32-byte) hash value stored as an array of 32 unsigned bytes. Intended to hold outputs of 256-bit hash functions. As a typedef to an array type, it decays to a pointer in many contexts; take care when passing to functions to avoid unintended pointer decay or sizeof mismatches.
No custom data types (structs, enums, typedefs, or classes) are defined in this header. It only declares the function hex_to_bytes and includes standard headers.

State/context object for streaming Base64 encoding and decoding. Tracks partial block bytes (num), line-length handling (length), a small buffer for pending input/output (enc_data), current processed line length (line_num), and whether a newline is expected (expect_nl). Used with base64_encode_* and base64_decode_* APIs. Construction is trivial: zero-initialize or call the corresponding _init function before use. Lifetime is managed by the caller; no dynamic allocation is performed by the context itself.
No structs, enums, typedefs, or classes are defined in this header. It only declares two functions (file_size and file_read_all). Therefore, there are no custom data types to document.

objects.description: Anonymous enumeration that defines integral identifiers for many object identifiers (OIDs) used in GMSSL, X.509, PKIX, and common crypto algorithms. The enum constants map symbolic names like OID_sm3, OID_sha256, OID_ce_key_usage, etc., to integer codes. There is no explicit typedef name; the constants have type int. Construction and lifetime are trivial; values are compile-time constants.

Preprocessor macros define several OID arc sequences (e.g., oid_pkix, oid_rsadsi, oid_at, oid_ce, oid_sm, etc.). These are not types but macros; thus no data type is defined here. Note: included to confirm there are no other structs/enums/typedefs/classes present. No constructible type exists for these macros.

SM3 hash computation context holding the internal chaining state, processed block count, partial block buffer, and number of bytes currently buffered. Used with sm3_init/update/finish for incremental hashing.
Context for HMAC-SM3 operations. Embeds an SM3 context and stores the (processed) key block. Use sm3_hmac_init/update/finish.
Context for SM3-based KDF streaming output. Tracks an internal SM3 context and desired output length. Use sm3_kdf_init/update/finish.

Flexible digest context that can operate as plain SM3 or HMAC-SM3 depending on initialization. Contains a union of SM3/HMAC contexts and a state flag to track mode/progress. Use sm3_digest_init/update/finish.

sm2_z256_t is a 256-bit unsigned integer stored as four 64-bit limbs; sm2_z512_t is a 512-bit integer stored as eight 64-bit limbs. They are used as the base big-integer representations for SM2 field and scalar arithmetic.

Jacobian projective point on the SM2 P-256 curve. Coordinates X, Y, Z are field elements modulo the SM2 prime. Z=0 represents the point at infinity. Used for point arithmetic, serialization, and scalar multiplication.
Affine point on the SM2 P-256 curve with coordinates (x, y) over the prime field. Used for interfacing with affine operations and precomputation tables.

Container for an SM2 key pair: a public key as an elliptic-curve point (SM2_Z256_POINT) and a private key scalar (sm2_z256_t). Used across signing, verification, encryption, decryption, and key exchange APIs. Exact ownership/lifetime of embedded fields is by value within the struct.
Fixed-size representation of an SM2 signature holding 32-byte big-endian r and s values. Used for raw sign/verify and conversion to/from DER.
Precomputation blob for fast SM2 signing. Stores ephemeral scalar k and its related x1 modulo n to accelerate repeated signing. Typically prepared in batches.
Stateful SM2 signature context integrating SM3 hashing, optional fast-sign precomputations, and precomputed public point tables. Supports init/update/finish workflows and fixed-length signatures.
Stateful SM2 verification context holding SM3 hash state, the public key, and a precomputed public point table for accelerated verification. Used with init/update/finish APIs.
Affine elliptic-curve point with 32-byte big-endian X and Y coordinates, used in ciphertext representation (C1) and related precomputations. Not the same as SM2_Z256_POINT (external type).
Structured SM2 ciphertext containing the ephemeral point C1, 32-byte hash (C3), and variable-length ciphertext (C2) with explicit size. Used for low-level encrypt/decrypt and DER conversions.
Precomputation record for SM2 encryption holding an ephemeral scalar k and its corresponding ephemeral point C1 to speed up repeated encrypt operations.
Streaming/context API for SM2 encryption maintaining a pool of precomputed values and a plaintext buffer for chunked updates before finalization.
Streaming/context API for SM2 decryption managing an internal ciphertext buffer for incremental input and final decryption using an SM2 private key.

A share of an SM2 private key for Shamir-style secret sharing. Each share embeds an SM2_KEY plus metadata: the share's 1-based index within the set and the total number of shares generated. Intended to be produced by sm2_key_split and consumed by sm2_key_recover. Details of SM2_KEY are defined in gmssl/sm2.h and not in this header. The constant SM2_KEY_MAX_SHARES limits total shares to 12. Construction and destruction are managed by the API functions; no special destructor is specified here.

Opaque type representing an SM2 digital signature. It is referenced in function parameters but not defined in this header. Its actual structure is defined elsewhere in the library; details unknown here.

Opaque type representing a point on the SM2 elliptic curve. It is referenced for output of recovered public key points but not defined in this header. Its structure is defined elsewhere; details unknown here.

objects.definition: typedef uint8_t sm2_bn_t[32];
objects.description: Fixed-size 256-bit big number buffer used by SM2 ring signature routines to hold scalars (e.g., r and s values). It is an array type alias with 32 bytes.

Context object for incremental SM2 ring signature generation and verification. Holds running SM3 hash state, the signer's private key, a collection of public keys forming the ring, and optional user identity (ID) data. Lifecycle: initialize with sm2_ring_sign_init or sm2_ring_verify_init; add signers via sm2_ring_sign_add_signer or sm2_ring_verify_add_signer; feed data with update; finalize with finish to produce or verify a signature. Internal memory ownership of id is not specified in this header; consult implementation to determine whether id is referenced or copied.

objects.definition: typedef uint64_t sm9_z256_t[4];
objects.description: 256-bit big integer type represented as four 64-bit limbs; used as base field element modulo the SM9 prime and as scalars modulo the group order. Stored in raw limb form; many APIs operate in Montgomery form when specified.

objects.definition: typedef sm9_z256_t sm9_z256_fp2_t[2];
objects.description: Quadratic extension field element over Fp, represented as two sm9_z256_t components (a + b·u). Used for twist curve coordinates and higher extensions.

objects.definition: typedef sm9_z256_fp2_t sm9_z256_fp4_t[2];
objects.description: Quartic extension field element over Fp constructed from two fp2 components (A + B·v). Used as building block of Fp12.

objects.definition: typedef sm9_z256_fp4_t sm9_z256_fp12_t[3];
objects.description: Degree-12 extension field element over Fp (target group of pairing), represented by three fp4 components; supports arithmetic, Frobenius maps, and exponentiation for final exponentiation.
Projective (likely Jacobian) point on E(Fp): y^2 = x^3 + 5. Coordinates are stored in Montgomery form. Provides operations for point arithmetic, serialization, and multiplication by scalars.
Affine point on E(Fp) with coordinates as four-limb 256-bit integers (non-Montgomery). Used as inputs to mixed addition and Miller line evaluation.
Projective point on the quadratic twist E'(Fp^2) used for SM9 pairings. Coordinates are fp2 elements; supports arithmetic, serialization, scalar multiplication, and automorphisms (pi1/pi2).

SM9 signing master key for identity-based signatures. Holds the master public key Ppubs on the twist curve and the master secret scalar ks. Used to derive per-identity signing private keys and to export the corresponding master public key.
Per-identity SM9 signing private key extracted from a signing master key. Contains the system master public key Ppubs and the user private point ds on the base curve.
SM9 signature object consisting of a hash scalar h and an elliptic curve point S. Used for encoding/decoding and verification of SM9 signatures.
Incremental hashing context for SM9 signing/verification built on SM3. Used with sm9_sign_* and sm9_verify_* streaming APIs.
SM9 encryption master key for identity-based encryption (and reused for key exchange). Contains the master public key Ppube on the base curve and the master secret scalar ke.

Per-identity SM9 encryption private key extracted from an encryption master key (also used for key exchange). Contains the system master public key Ppube and the user private point de on the twist curve.

Expanded AES key schedule object holding round keys (rk) and number of rounds for AES-128/192/256. Used with encrypt/decrypt and AEAD/mode APIs in this header. The struct is fully defined and may be stack- or heap-allocated, but should be initialized via the provided key setup functions before use.

Opaque-ish state object for the ChaCha20 stream cipher. Holds the 16-word (512-bit) working state used to generate keystream blocks per RFC 8439. The layout suggests little-endian 32-bit words stored in d[16]. Used with chacha20_init to set key/nonce/counter, then chacha20_generate_keystream to produce keystream bytes.

objects.definition: typedef uint64_t gf128_t[2];
objects.description: Binary-field element type representing an element of GF(2^128) under the reduction polynomial x^128 + x^7 + x^2 + x + 1. Implemented as an array of two 64-bit words (little-endian word order implied by common practice, but exact byte order is determined by the from/to functions). Operations on this type are provided by the accompanying gf128_* API functions. Memory for gf128_t is typically stack- or statically-allocated since it is a fixed-size array type; no special destructor is required.

GHASH context for incremental computation of the GCM GHASH authentication subkey operation. Holds the hash subkey H, current accumulator X, processed lengths for AAD and ciphertext, a 16-byte partial block buffer, and a byte count. Intended to be initialized with ghash_init, updated with ghash_update, and finalized with ghash_finish to produce the 16-byte tag. Details of gf128_t are defined in gmssl/gf128.h and not in this header.

Opaque-forward-declared then defined structure describing a block cipher algorithm descriptor. Contains metadata (OID, key and block sizes) and function pointers for key setup and single-block encryption/decryption. Instances represent algorithms (e.g., SM4, AES-128), not per-key state.

Per-key context for a block cipher. Holds algorithm-specific expanded key material (SM4_KEY or AES_KEY in the union) and a pointer to the associated BLOCK_CIPHER descriptor indicating which algorithm the key is for.

objects.definition: typedef void (*block_cipher_set_encrypt_key_func)(BLOCK_CIPHER_KEY *key, const uint8_t *raw_key);
objects.description: Function pointer type for setting up an encryption key schedule into a BLOCK_CIPHER_KEY from a raw key byte array.

objects.definition: typedef void (*block_cipher_set_decrypt_key_func)(BLOCK_CIPHER_KEY *key, const uint8_t *raw_key);
objects.description: Function pointer type for setting up a decryption key schedule into a BLOCK_CIPHER_KEY from a raw key byte array.

objects.definition: typedef void (*block_cipher_encrypt_func)(const BLOCK_CIPHER_KEY *key, const uint8_t *in, uint8_t *out);
objects.description: Function pointer type for encrypting one block: reads a single block from in and writes the ciphertext block to out using the provided key context.

objects.definition: typedef void (*block_cipher_decrypt_func)(const BLOCK_CIPHER_KEY *key, const uint8_t *in, uint8_t *out);
objects.description: Function pointer type for decrypting one block: reads a single block from in and writes the plaintext block to out using the provided key context.
Round-key schedule for the SM4 block cipher. Holds 32 32-bit round keys derived from a 128-bit raw key. Must be initialized with sm4_set_encrypt_key or sm4_set_decrypt_key before use.
Context for SM4 in CBC mode with PKCS#7-style padding via the *_finish APIs. Maintains an SM4 key schedule, IV, partial block buffer, and buffered length.
Context for SM4 in CTR and CTR32 modes. Stores key schedule, counter block, keystream buffer, and buffered byte count.
Context for SM4-GCM authenticated encryption. Combines SM4-CTR encryption with GHASH authentication. Tracks computed Y value, tag length, MAC buffer/length, and total encrypted length.

Context object for computing an SM4-based CBC-MAC. Holds an SM4_KEY schedule, a 16-byte IV buffer, and its effective length. Used with sm4_cbc_mac_init/update/finish to produce a 16-byte MAC. Internal field SM4_KEY is defined in gmssl/sm4.h and not in this header.

Context object that combines SM4-CBC encryption state and SM3-HMAC authentication state to implement an encrypt-then-MAC AEAD-like construction. It holds an SM4 CBC context (enc_ctx), an SM3 HMAC context (mac_ctx), a buffer for the computed MAC (mac), and the MAC length (maclen). Construction and lifecycle are driven by the init/update/finish functions in this header. Internal member types (SM4_CBC_CTX, SM3_HMAC_CTX) are defined in their respective headers and are not detailed here.

OpenCL-backed SM4 cipher context holding round keys and OpenCL resources (context, command queue, program, kernel, and buffers) used to perform SM4 operations on a device. The struct owns these OpenCL handles for the lifetime of the context. Details such as workgroup size are not specified here.

Context type combining SM4 in CTR mode for encryption/decryption and SM3 HMAC for authentication. Holds an SM4 CTR context (enc_ctx), an SM3 HMAC context (mac_ctx), the computed MAC buffer (mac) of size SM3_HMAC_SIZE, and the current MAC length (maclen). Intended for use with the provided encrypt/decrypt init/update/finish APIs implementing an AEAD-like scheme using key material of 48 bytes (32 bytes for HMAC key + 16 bytes for SM4 key, inferred) and a 16-byte IV.

Opaque-ish HMAC context structure holding the selected message digest algorithm pointer and three digest contexts: the working digest context, and inner/outer keyed contexts for HMAC processing. Used with hmac_init/update/finish to compute HMACs. Details of DIGEST and DIGEST_CTX are defined elsewhere.

Opaque digest algorithm descriptor type referenced from gmssl/hmac.h. It is only referenced here; no definition is provided in this header. Details such as fields and lifecycle are unknown from this file.
No custom structs, enums, typedefs, or classes are defined in this header. The only symbols introduced are function declarations. There are no type aliases to document.
No structs, enums, typedefs, or classes are defined in this header. It only declares two functions (pem_read, pem_write). Therefore there are no custom data types to document.

Algorithm vtable for message-digest implementations. Holds OID and size metadata plus function pointers to init/update/finish a DIGEST_CTX. Used to select concrete algorithms (e.g., SM3, SHA-2 variants).

Opaque-ish per-operation state for a digest computation. Contains a union of concrete hash contexts and a pointer to the selected DIGEST vtable. Must be initialized with digest_init and used via digest_update/digest_finish.
Enumeration of X.509 certificate version numbers as they appear in TBSCertificate.version (v1..v3).

Typedef for an enum describing high-level intended certificate usages/roles (server/client auth, key encipherment, CA, root CA, CRL signing). Used with x509_cert_check to validate certificate properties.
Typedef for an enum identifying the context of a certificate chain (server or client). Used by x509_certs_verify and related functions to apply role-specific validation rules.

No custom structs, enums, typedefs, or classes are defined in this header file. The file only declares functions for encoding, decoding, printing, and handling X.509 certification requests. All referenced types (e.g., SM2_KEY) are declared in other headers.

objects.definition:
#ifndef GMSSL_X509_H
#define GMSSL_X509_H

#include <gmssl/x509_cer.h>

#endif
objects.description: This header is an umbrella/include-only header that re-exports definitions from <gmssl/x509_cer.h>. It defines no custom types (structs, enums, typedefs, or classes) itself. The only content is a header guard and an include directive.
Anonymous enumeration defining CMS version constants. Only CMS_version_v1 is defined with value 1. As an enum, its pointer type when referenced is int *.

Holds a set of certificates and an associated SM2 signing private key used when creating CMS SignedData or SignedAndEnvelopedData. Fields: certs is a DER-encoded SET OF Certificate blob, certs_len its length, and sign_key is the SM2_KEY used to sign. The header provides no lifecycle functions for this struct; caller is responsible for allocating/freeing certs buffer and managing the SM2_KEY lifetime. Exact ownership semantics for sign_key are not documented here.

objects.definition: typedef uint32_t ZUC_BIT;
objects.description: Alias for a single ZUC direction/bit flag encoded in a 32-bit unsigned integer. Used in EEA/EIA APIs for the direction parameter.

objects.definition: typedef uint32_t ZUC_UINT5;
objects.description: Alias for a 5-bit value stored in a 32-bit unsigned integer. Used for the bearer parameter in EEA/EIA APIs.

objects.definition: typedef uint8_t  ZUC_UINT6;
objects.description: Alias for a 6-bit value stored in an 8-bit unsigned integer.

objects.definition: typedef uint32_t ZUC_UINT15;
objects.description: Alias for a 15-bit value stored in a 32-bit unsigned integer.

objects.definition: typedef uint32_t ZUC_UINT31;
objects.description: Alias for a 31-bit value stored in a 32-bit unsigned integer. Used for ZUC LFSR elements.

objects.definition: typedef uint32_t ZUC_UINT32;
objects.description: Alias for a 32-bit unsigned integer used across ZUC APIs.
Internal ZUC stream cipher state containing the 16-stage LFSR and two 32-bit registers R1 and R2. Used for key/IV setup and keystream generation.
Context for 32-bit ZUC MAC (EIA3) computation. Maintains ZUC state plus MAC accumulator (T), subkey (K0), and a small buffering area.
Context for ZUC-256 MAC computation supporting variable MAC sizes. Extends the base ZUC state with 128-bit accumulators/subkeys and buffering metadata including desired MAC length in bits.
High-level streaming encryption context for ZUC, encapsulating a ZUC_STATE and a 4-byte partial block buffer for byte-wise processing.

Opaque cross-platform socket handle type used by this header's API. On Windows it aliases SOCKET; on POSIX it aliases int. Use with the tls_socket_* functions/macros. Lifetime is managed by tls_socket_create/tls_socket_close and related functions.
Return type for send/recv-like operations to capture byte counts or error codes in a platform-neutral way. On Windows it's int; on POSIX it's ssize_t.
Socket length type for address/option length parameters, abstracted across platforms. On Windows it's int; on POSIX it's socklen_t.

Alias for an unsigned 8-bit integer type defined by stdint.h. Included here only because it appears in the function signature; this header does not define it. Per instructions, types merely referenced but not defined should be ignored. No custom data types are defined in this header.
No structs, enums, typedefs, classes, or other custom data types are defined in this header. It only declares functions rdrand_bytes and, conditionally, rdseed_bytes.

objects.definition: typedef uint32_t uint24_t;
objects.description: Typedef alias representing a 24-bit unsigned integer stored in a 32-bit container. Used for TLS 24-bit length fields and similar encodings.
Enumeration of supported TLS/SSL/DTLS protocol version codes.

typedef enum  {
	TLS_handshake_hello_request		= 0,

SHA-1 hashing context holding the internal state words, processed block count, the current partial input block buffer, and the number of bytes currently buffered. Used with sha1_init, sha1_update, and sha1_finish to compute a SHA-1 digest.

SHA-224 hash context. Maintains intermediate state, processed block count, a working block buffer, and the number of buffered bytes. Initialize with sha224_init, feed data with sha224_update, and finalize with sha224_finish.
SHA-256 hash context. Holds the internal chaining state, total processed block count, the current 64-byte block buffer, and the buffered length. Use sha256_init, sha256_update, and sha256_finish.
SHA-384 hash context. 64-bit word state with a 128-byte block buffer and counters. Use sha384_init, sha384_update, and sha384_finish.
SHA-512 hash context. 64-bit word state, 128-byte working block, and counters. Use sha512_init, sha512_update, and sha512_finish.

HMAC-SHA256 context. Wraps an inner SHA256 context and stores a block-sized key material buffer. Initialize with sha256_hmac_init, update with sha256_hmac_update, and finalize with sha256_hmac_finish.

The header provides no additional documentation.

functions.name: gmssl_version_num

functions.description: Returns the library version number as an integer code. Typically used to programmatically check the linked GmSSL version at runtime. Based on the header, this likely corresponds to the GMSSL_VERSION_NUM macro (e.g., 30103 for version 3.1.3).
requirements: No arguments are required.
No error reporting is documented; callers should treat the return value as a non-negative integer version code.
Behavior does not require prior initialization per the header; no stateful preconditions are indicated.

functions.name: gmssl_version_str

functions.description: Returns a pointer to a read-only, null-terminated C string describing the library version (e.g., "GmSSL 3.1.3 Dev"), suitable for display or logging. Intended for human-readable version checks or diagnostics.
requirements: The returned pointer refers to immutable storage; the caller must not modify the string.
The returned pointer must not be freed by the caller.
The returned value is expected to be a valid null-terminated C string; no error reporting is documented.
No initialization or specific call order is indicated by the header.

functions.name: memxor
functions.signature: void memxor(void *r, const void *a, size_t len);
functions.description: XORs len bytes from buffer a into buffer r, writing the result to r. Typical usage is to in-place XOR an existing buffer (r) with another buffer (a) of the same length. Details about whether overlapping regions beyond r serving as both input and output are supported are not documented; behavior with other overlaps is unknown.
requirements: r must point to a writable buffer of at least len bytes.
a must point to a readable buffer of at least len bytes.
The function does not return a value; callers cannot detect errors via return code.
Whether overlapping memory regions (other than r being both source/destination) are supported is unknown; avoid overlapping r with a unless the implementation explicitly permits it.
Pointer arguments should be valid and non-NULL when len > 0; behavior for NULL with len == 0 is unspecified.

functions.name: gmssl_memxor
functions.signature: void gmssl_memxor(void *r, const void *a, const void *b, size_t len);
functions.description: Computes the byte-wise XOR of len bytes from buffers a and b and stores the result into buffer r. Intended for combining two equal-length buffers without leaking through branch timing. No explicit documentation is provided here on overlap semantics.
requirements: r must point to a writable buffer of at least len bytes.
a and b must each point to readable buffers of at least len bytes.
The function does not return a value; callers cannot detect errors via return code.
Overlap behavior between r and a/b is not documented; to be safe, ensure r does not overlap with a or b.
Pointer arguments should be valid and non-NULL when len > 0; behavior for NULL with len == 0 is unspecified.

functions.name: gmssl_secure_memcmp
functions.signature: int gmssl_secure_memcmp(const volatile void * volatile in_a, const volatile void * volatile in_b, size_t len);
functions.description: Performs a constant-time comparison of two buffers a and b over len bytes to mitigate timing side channels. Commonly returns 0 if the memory regions are equal and non-zero otherwise; exact non-zero value semantics are not specified in this header. Volatile qualifiers are used to discourage compiler optimizations that could affect timing.
requirements: in_a and in_b must each point to readable memory regions of at least len bytes.
Designed to run in time that does not depend on the buffer contents; callers should not assume early exit.
Return value is int; typical convention is 0 on equality and non-zero otherwise, but exact values beyond equality are unspecified.
Pointer arguments should be valid and non-NULL when len > 0; behavior for NULL with len == 0 is unspecified.

functions.name: gmssl_secure_clear
functions.signature: void gmssl_secure_clear(void *ptr, size_t len);
functions.description: Securely clears (e.g., zeroes) len bytes of memory at ptr in a way intended to prevent the compiler from optimizing the operation away, to clear sensitive data. No return value.
requirements: ptr must point to a writable buffer of at least len bytes.
Intended for clearing sensitive data; ensure ptr points to memory that can be safely overwritten.
Pointer should be valid and non-NULL when len > 0; behavior for NULL with len == 0 is unspecified.
Callers should not rely on this function to deallocate memory; it only overwrites contents.

functions.name: mem_is_zero
functions.signature: int mem_is_zero(const uint8_t *buf, size_t len);
functions.description: Checks whether the len-byte buffer buf consists entirely of zero bytes. The header suggests a potential future change to accept void* instead of uint8_t*. The exact return convention is not documented here; it is typically 1 if all bytes are zero and 0 otherwise.
requirements: buf must point to a readable buffer of at least len bytes.
Return value semantics beyond the typical convention are not explicitly documented in this header; callers should verify expected values if available in implementation/docs.
Pointer should be valid and non-NULL when len > 0; behavior for NULL with len == 0 is unspecified.

functions.name: print_der

requirements: in must point to a readable memory buffer of at least inlen bytes; undefined behavior if not.
If inlen is greater than 0, in should not be NULL.
inlen may be 0 to represent an empty buffer; behavior is otherwise unspecified.
No return value; callers cannot detect errors via return code.

functions.name: print_bytes
functions.signature: void print_bytes(const uint8_t *in, size_t inlen);

requirements: in must point to a readable memory buffer of at least inlen bytes.
If inlen is greater than 0, in should not be NULL.
inlen may be 0 to represent an empty buffer; behavior is otherwise unspecified.

requirements: in must point to a readable array of at least inlen elements of type uint32_t.
If inlen is greater than 0, in should not be NULL.
inlen counts elements, not bytes.
No return value; callers cannot detect errors via return code.

functions.name: format_print
functions.signature: int format_print(FILE *fp, int format, int indent, const char *str, ...);
functions.description: Formats and prints a message to the given FILE stream with an indentation level and a format/style controlled by format flags. Likely supports GMSSL_FMT_BIN/HEX/DER/PEM and FMT_CARRAY styles and includes a printf-like message prefix given by str and its varargs. Exact return value semantics and specific formatting behavior are not documented here and are unknown.
requirements: fp must be a valid, writable FILE* (opened for output).
format is an integer bitmask; expected flags include GMSSL_FMT_BIN, GMSSL_FMT_HEX, GMSSL_FMT_DER, GMSSL_FMT_PEM, and FMT_CARRAY; behavior for unsupported values is unknown.
indent should be non-negative; behavior for negative values is unspecified.
str must be a non-NULL printf-style format string when varargs are provided; provided varargs must match the format specifiers in str.
Thread-safety is not guaranteed; do not call concurrently on the same FILE* unless externally synchronized.
Return value is int; success/failure convention is not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: format_bytes
functions.signature: int format_bytes(FILE *fp, int format, int indent, const char *str, const uint8_t *data, size_t datalen);
functions.description: Formats and prints a label/prefix (str) and a byte buffer (data, datalen) to the given FILE stream according to the specified format flags and indentation. Intended to render binary data in binary/hex/DER/PEM/C array styles for debugging or logging. Exact return value and precise formatting are not documented here and are unknown.
requirements: fp must be a valid, writable FILE*.
format is an integer bitmask; expected flags include GMSSL_FMT_BIN, GMSSL_FMT_HEX, GMSSL_FMT_DER, GMSSL_FMT_PEM, and FMT_CARRAY; behavior for unsupported values is unknown.
indent should be non-negative.
str should be non-NULL if a label or prefix is expected; behavior with NULL is unspecified.
data must point to a readable buffer of at least datalen bytes; if datalen > 0, data must not be NULL.
datalen may be 0 to represent an empty buffer; handling is unspecified.
Return value is int; success/failure convention is not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: format_string
functions.signature: int format_string(FILE *fp, int format, int indent, const char *str, const uint8_t *data, size_t datalen);
functions.description: Formats and prints a label/prefix (str) and a byte string (data, datalen) to the given FILE stream with the specified formatting flags and indentation. Intended for rendering textual or byte-string data in various formats (e.g., PEM, hex). Exact output details and return value semantics are not documented here and are unknown.
requirements: fp must be a valid, writable FILE*.
format is an integer bitmask; expected flags include GMSSL_FMT_BIN, GMSSL_FMT_HEX, GMSSL_FMT_DER, GMSSL_FMT_PEM, and FMT_CARRAY; behavior for unsupported values is unknown.
indent should be non-negative.
str should be non-NULL if a label or prefix is expected; behavior with NULL is unspecified.
data must point to a readable buffer of at least datalen bytes; if datalen > 0, data must not be NULL.
datalen may be 0 to represent an empty string; encoding/interpretation of data as text vs bytes is unspecified.
Return value is int; success/failure convention is not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: hex_to_bytes
functions.signature: int hex_to_bytes(const char *in, size_t inlen, uint8_t *out, size_t *outlen);
functions.description: Convert a hex-encoded byte sequence into raw bytes. The function reads up to inlen characters from in, decodes them, and writes the resulting bytes to out while reporting the number of output bytes via outlen. Typical usage is to pass a pointer to the hex data and its length, provide an output buffer, and retrieve the decoded length through outlen. Return value semantics are not documented here; treat the int as a status code where non-success indicates a decoding failure or invalid input. Details such as accepted whitespace, case sensitivity, and exact return conventions are unknown based solely on this header and are inferred from common library patterns.
requirements: in must be non-NULL and point to at least inlen readable bytes.

outlen must be non-NULL; on success it will be set to the number of decoded bytes. (Exact in/out contract is not documented; common pattern is that *outlen may be used as input capacity and is set to the actual length on return.)

If out is non-NULL, it must point to a buffer large enough to hold the decoded bytes. A safe capacity estimate is at least inlen/2 bytes when input contains only hex digits. (Inferred from typical hex encoding.)

Input should consist of valid hexadecimal characters representing bytes (commonly 0-9, a-f, A-F). Presence and handling of whitespace, separators, or prefixes like "0x" are unknown; for portability, provide only contiguous hex digits. (Inferred)
If the API uses *outlen as input capacity (common pattern), initialize *outlen to the size of the output buffer before calling; check and use the updated value after a successful return. (Inferred)
Callers must check the return value before using the output; on failure, the contents of out and/or *outlen may be unspecified. (Inferred)
If in represents pure hex digits without separators, inlen should be even so that two hex characters map to one byte; odd lengths may cause failure. (Inferred)

functions.name: base64_encode_init
functions.signature: void base64_encode_init(BASE64_CTX *ctx);
functions.description: Initializes a BASE64_CTX for streaming Base64 encoding. Call this once before any base64_encode_update calls, then finish with base64_encode_finish. Resets internal counters and buffering state.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a BASE64_CTX storage provided by the caller.
Call this before any base64_encode_update or base64_encode_finish using the same ctx.
Do not reuse the same ctx concurrently from multiple threads without external synchronization.
Reinitialize (call base64_encode_init again) before starting a new, separate encoding stream with the same ctx.

functions.name: base64_encode_update
functions.signature: int base64_encode_update(BASE64_CTX *ctx, const uint8_t *in, int inlen, uint8_t *out, int *outlen);
functions.description: Consumes a chunk of input bytes and produces Base64-encoded output using the ongoing ctx state. Can be called repeatedly to encode a stream. Writes encoded bytes to out and stores the number of bytes written in *outlen. Return value semantics are not documented here; treat nonzero/zero as unknown and check implementation or library docs.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, initialized BASE64_CTX (initialized via base64_encode_init).
in must point to at least inlen readable bytes; if inlen is 0, behavior for in==NULL is unknown.
out must point to a writable buffer; outlen must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an int.

Caller must provide sufficient space in out. For a complete message of length L, a safe upper bound is BASE64_ENCODE_LENGTH(L). For incremental calls, ensure enough space based on worst-case expansion (~4/3 of input plus possible line breaks); exact per-call maximum is not specified.
outlen is set by the function to the number of bytes written; caller should not assume any specific relation between inlen and *outlen for partial blocks.
Do not use the same ctx concurrently from multiple threads.
Preserve ctx between successive update calls and the final finish call without modifying its internals.

functions.name: base64_encode_finish
functions.signature: void base64_encode_finish(BASE64_CTX *ctx, uint8_t *out, int *outlen);
functions.description: Finalizes the Base64 encoding stream, flushing any buffered bytes and emitting any required padding or trailing data. Writes any remaining encoded output to out and stores the number of bytes written in *outlen. Does not return a status code.
requirements: ctx must be a valid BASE64_CTX previously initialized with base64_encode_init and used with base64_encode_update.
out must point to a writable buffer; outlen must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an int.

Caller must provide sufficient space in out to hold any remaining output. If the total input length across all updates is L, using BASE64_ENCODE_LENGTH(L) overall is safe; the finish step typically emits at most a small number of bytes (unknown exact bound).
Do not call finish before at least initializing the context; calling multiple times per stream is unsupported unless the stream is reinitialized.
Do not use the same ctx concurrently from multiple threads.

functions.name: base64_decode_init
functions.signature: void base64_decode_init(BASE64_CTX *ctx);
functions.description: Initializes a BASE64_CTX for streaming Base64 decoding. Call this once before any base64_decode_update calls, then finish with base64_decode_finish. Resets internal decoding state, including line handling.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a BASE64_CTX storage provided by the caller.
Call this before any base64_decode_update or base64_decode_finish using the same ctx.
Do not reuse the same ctx concurrently from multiple threads without external synchronization.
Reinitialize (call base64_decode_init again) before starting a new, separate decoding stream with the same ctx.

functions.name: base64_decode_update
functions.signature: int base64_decode_update(BASE64_CTX *ctx, const uint8_t *in, int inlen, uint8_t *out, int *outlen);
functions.description: Consumes a chunk of Base64-encoded input and produces decoded binary output using the ongoing ctx state. Can be called repeatedly for streaming decode. Writes decoded bytes to out and stores the number of bytes written in *outlen. Return value semantics are not documented here; treat nonzero/zero as unknown and check implementation or library docs.

functions.signature: int sm2_key_split(const SM2_KEY *key, size_t recover_cnt, size_t total_cnt, SM2_KEY_SHARE *shares)
functions.description: Split an SM2 private key into multiple Shamir secret shares. The caller specifies the threshold recover_cnt (minimum number of shares required to reconstruct) and the total number of shares total_cnt. On success, the array shares is populated with total_cnt SM2_KEY_SHARE items containing per-share material and metadata (index and total count). Typical usage: initialize/provide a valid SM2_KEY, allocate an array of SM2_KEY_SHARE of length total_cnt, and call this function with desired threshold and total shares. Return value semantics are not explicitly documented here; in GmSSL-style APIs, 1 usually indicates success and 0/negative indicates failure, but this is not guaranteed by this header.
requirements: key must point to a valid, initialized SM2_KEY containing the secret to be split
recover_cnt must be a positive integer and must not exceed total_cnt (inferred from threshold sharing semantics)
total_cnt must be a positive integer and must not exceed SM2_KEY_MAX_SHARES (12)
shares must point to a writable array with capacity for at least total_cnt SM2_KEY_SHARE elements
Caller should not reuse or leak generated share secrets; handle output shares as sensitive material

kbuf must be a buffer of at least klen bytes to receive the derived key.

functions.signature: int sm9_do_encrypt(const SM9_ENC_MASTER_KEY *mpk, const char *id, size_t idlen, const uint8_t *in, size_t inlen, SM9_Z256_POINT *C1, uint8_t *c2, uint8_t c3[SM3_HMAC_SIZE]);
functions.description: Low-level SM9 public-key encryption: encrypts plaintext in to components (C1, c2, c3), where C1 is an EC point, c2 is XOR-encrypted data, and c3 is a 32-byte HMAC-SM3 tag.
requirements: mpk must contain a valid Ppube.
id must be the recipient identity; idlen must match its length.
in must point to plaintext of length inlen; inlen must not exceed SM9_MAX_PLAINTEXT_SIZE (macro states 255).
C1 must be non-NULL to receive the EC point.
c2 must point to a buffer of at least inlen bytes (ciphertext component).
c3 must point to a buffer of size SM3_HMAC_SIZE (32 bytes).

functions.description: Low-level SM9 public-key decryption: verifies c3 and decrypts c2 using the recipient’s private key and EC point C1, writing plaintext to out.
requirements: key must be a valid SM9 encryption private key.
id must be the recipient identity; idlen must match its length.
C1 must point to the EC point from encryption.
c2 must point to the ciphertext component; c2len is its length.
c3 must point to SM3_HMAC_SIZE (32) bytes.
out must point to a buffer of at least c2len bytes to receive plaintext.

functions.description: Encodes SM9 ciphertext components (C1, c2, c3) into a DER-encoded SM9Cipher structure and appends to out.
requirements: C1 must point to the EC point component.
c2 must point to the XOR-encrypted data; c2len is its length.
c3 must be a 32-byte HMAC-SM3 tag (SM3_HMAC_SIZE).
out and outlen must be non-NULL with sufficient space; on success they are updated.
Total output should not exceed SM9_MAX_CIPHERTEXT_SIZE (macro 367) when using maximum sizes.

functions.name: sm9_ciphertext_from_der
functions.signature: int sm9_ciphertext_from_der(SM9_Z256_POINT *C1, const uint8_t **c2, size_t *c2len, const uint8_t **c3, const uint8_t **in, size_t *inlen);
functions.description: Parses a DER-encoded SM9Cipher into its components C1, c2 pointer/length, and c3 pointer, advancing the input on success.
requirements: C1 must be non-NULL and writable.
c2, c2len, and c3 must be non-NULL pointers to receive pointers/lengths into the input buffer.
in and inlen must be non-NULL; on success *in advanced and *inlen reduced.
The lifetime of the returned c2 and c3 pointers is tied to the input buffer; do not free them separately.

functions.name: sm9_ciphertext_print
functions.signature: int sm9_ciphertext_print(FILE *fp, int fmt, int ind, const char *label, const uint8_t *a, size_t alen);

a must point to the encoded ciphertext; alen must match its size.
fmt, ind, label control formatting (not specified).

functions.name: sm9_encrypt
functions.signature: int sm9_encrypt(const SM9_ENC_MASTER_KEY *mpk, const char *id, size_t idlen, const uint8_t *in, size_t inlen, uint8_t *out, size_t *outlen);
functions.description: High-level SM9 encryption: encrypts input bytes into a single DER-encoded SM9Cipher stored in out.
requirements: mpk must contain a valid Ppube.
id must be the recipient identity; idlen must match its length.
in must point to plaintext of length inlen; inlen must not exceed SM9_MAX_PLAINTEXT_SIZE (255).
out must be a buffer large enough to hold the DER-encoded ciphertext; maximum indicated by SM9_MAX_CIPHERTEXT_SIZE (367).
outlen must be non-NULL; on success set to number of bytes written.

functions.name: sm9_decrypt
functions.signature: int sm9_decrypt(const SM9_ENC_KEY *key, const char *id, size_t idlen, const uint8_t *in, size_t inlen, uint8_t *out, size_t *outlen);

requirements: key must be a valid SM9 encryption private key.
id must be the recipient identity; idlen must match its length.
in must point to a DER-encoded SM9Cipher of length inlen.
out must be a buffer large enough to hold the recovered plaintext (up to SM9_MAX_PLAINTEXT_SIZE).
outlen must be non-NULL to receive the output length.

functions.name: sm9_exch_master_key_extract_key

functions.name: sm9_exch_step_1A
functions.signature: int sm9_exch_step_1A(const SM9_EXCH_MASTER_KEY *mpk, const char *idB, size_t idBlen, SM9_Z256_POINT *RA, sm9_z256_t rA);
functions.description: SM9 key exchange step 1 for party A: generates an ephemeral value rA and corresponding EC point RA for peer B’s identity using the master public key.
requirements: mpk must contain a valid master public key for exchange (alias of encryption mpk).
idB must be B’s identity; idBlen must match its length.
RA must be non-NULL and writable to receive the EC point.

functions.name: sm9_exch_step_1B
functions.signature: int sm9_exch_step_1B(const SM9_EXCH_MASTER_KEY *mpk, const char *idA, size_t idAlen, const char *idB, size_t idBlen, const SM9_EXCH_KEY *key, const SM9_Z256_POINT *RA, SM9_Z256_POINT *RB, uint8_t *sk, size_t klen);

functions.name: sm9_exch_step_2A
functions.signature: int sm9_exch_step_2A(const SM9_EXCH_MASTER_KEY *mpk, const char *idA, size_t idAlen, const char *idB, size_t idBlen, const SM9_EXCH_KEY *key, const sm9_z256_t rA, const SM9_Z256_POINT *RA, const SM9_Z256_POINT *RB, uint8_t *sk, size_t klen);
functions.description: SM9 key exchange step 2 for party A: uses its ephemeral rA and points (RA, RB) with its exchange key to derive the shared secret sk of length klen.

key must be A’s valid exchange private key.
rA must contain A’s ephemeral scalar from step 1.

functions.name: sm9_exch_step_2B
functions.signature: int sm9_exch_step_2B();
functions.description: Placeholder for SM9 key exchange step 2 for party B; declared but no parameters are defined in this header. Likely completes the exchange on B’s side.

functions.name: aes_set_encrypt_key
functions.signature: int aes_set_encrypt_key(AES_KEY *key, const uint8_t *raw_key, size_t raw_key_len);
functions.description: Initializes an AES_KEY for encryption from a raw AES key. Use this before calling aes_encrypt, aes_cbc_encrypt, aes_cbc_padding_encrypt, aes_ctr_encrypt, or aes_gcm_* for encryption operations. The key length determines AES-128/192/256.
requirements: key must be a valid, writable pointer to an AES_KEY structure
raw_key must point to a buffer containing the raw AES key bytes
raw_key_len must be exactly 16, 24, or 32 bytes (AES128_KEY_SIZE, AES192_KEY_SIZE, AES256_KEY_SIZE)
The function returns an int; exact success/failure convention is unknown (not specified in header)

requirements: key must be a valid, writable pointer to an AES_KEY structure
raw_key must point to a buffer containing the raw AES key bytes
raw_key_len must be exactly 16, 24, or 32 bytes (AES128_KEY_SIZE, AES192_KEY_SIZE, AES256_KEY_SIZE)
The function returns an int; exact success/failure convention is unknown (not specified in header)

functions.name: aes_encrypt
functions.signature: void aes_encrypt(const AES_KEY *key, const uint8_t in[AES_BLOCK_SIZE], uint8_t out[AES_BLOCK_SIZE]);
functions.description: Encrypts one 16-byte block with AES in ECB mode using a pre-initialized encryption key schedule.
requirements: key must have been initialized for encryption via aes_set_encrypt_key
in must point to at least AES_BLOCK_SIZE (16) bytes of plaintext
out must point to at least AES_BLOCK_SIZE (16) bytes of writable memory
in and out may alias or be distinct; aliasing behavior not specified (unknown)

functions.name: aes_decrypt
functions.signature: void aes_decrypt(const AES_KEY *key, const uint8_t in[AES_BLOCK_SIZE], uint8_t out[AES_BLOCK_SIZE]);

requirements: key must have been initialized for decryption via aes_set_decrypt_key
in must point to at least AES_BLOCK_SIZE (16) bytes of ciphertext
out must point to at least AES_BLOCK_SIZE (16) bytes of writable memory
in and out may alias or be distinct; aliasing behavior not specified (unknown)

functions.name: aes_cbc_encrypt
functions.signature: void aes_cbc_encrypt(const AES_KEY *key, const uint8_t iv[AES_BLOCK_SIZE], const uint8_t *in, size_t nblocks, uint8_t *out);
functions.description: Encrypts nblocks of data in AES-CBC mode without padding. Processes exactly nblocks*16 bytes from in to out using the provided IV.
requirements: key must have been initialized for encryption via aes_set_encrypt_key
iv must point to AES_BLOCK_SIZE (16) bytes
in must point to at least nblocks * AES_BLOCK_SIZE bytes of input
out must point to at least nblocks * AES_BLOCK_SIZE bytes of writable memory
nblocks specifies the exact number of 16-byte blocks; input length must be an integral number of blocks
This function does not apply padding; caller must manage data length accordingly

functions.name: aes_cbc_decrypt
functions.signature: void aes_cbc_decrypt(const AES_KEY *key, const uint8_t iv[AES_BLOCK_SIZE], const uint8_t *in, size_t nblocks, uint8_t *out);
functions.description: Decrypts nblocks of data in AES-CBC mode without padding. Processes exactly nblocks*16 bytes from in to out using the provided IV.
requirements: key must have been initialized for decryption via aes_set_decrypt_key
iv must point to AES_BLOCK_SIZE (16) bytes
in must point to at least nblocks * AES_BLOCK_SIZE bytes of input
out must point to at least nblocks * AES_BLOCK_SIZE bytes of writable memory
nblocks specifies the exact number of 16-byte blocks; input length must be an integral number of blocks
This function does not remove padding; caller must handle padding if present

functions.name: aes_cbc_padding_encrypt
functions.signature: int aes_cbc_padding_encrypt(const AES_KEY *key, const uint8_t iv[AES_BLOCK_SIZE], const uint8_t *in, size_t inlen, uint8_t *out, size_t *outlen);
functions.description: Encrypts data in AES-CBC mode with padding (likely PKCS#7). Accepts arbitrary-length plaintext and outputs ciphertext padded to a multiple of 16 bytes. Writes the resulting ciphertext length to outlen.
requirements: key must have been initialized for encryption via aes_set_encrypt_key
iv must point to AES_BLOCK_SIZE (16) bytes
in must point to inlen bytes of plaintext (inlen may be zero)
out must point to a buffer large enough for inlen + AES_BLOCK_SIZE bytes (worst-case with padding)
outlen must be a valid, writable pointer; on success it receives the ciphertext length (a multiple of AES_BLOCK_SIZE)
The function returns an int; exact success/failure convention is unknown (not specified in header)
Padding scheme is not explicitly documented; assumed standard PKCS#7 based on naming (details unknown)

functions.name: aes_cbc_padding_decrypt
functions.signature: int aes_cbc_padding_decrypt(const AES_KEY *key, const uint8_t iv[AES_BLOCK_SIZE], const uint8_t *in, size_t inlen, uint8_t *out, size_t *outlen);
functions.description: Decrypts data in AES-CBC mode and removes padding (likely PKCS#7). Validates and strips padding, writing the plaintext and its length to out/outlen.
requirements: key must have been initialized for decryption via aes_set_decrypt_key
iv must point to AES_BLOCK_SIZE (16) bytes
in must point to inlen bytes of ciphertext
inlen must be a positive multiple of AES_BLOCK_SIZE (padding-based decryption requires full blocks)
out must point to a buffer large enough for inlen bytes (plaintext will be <= inlen)
outlen must be a valid, writable pointer; on success it receives the plaintext length
If padding is invalid, the function will fail; exact return convention is unknown (not specified in header)
Padding scheme is not explicitly documented; assumed standard PKCS#7 based on naming (details unknown)

functions.name: aes_ctr_encrypt
functions.signature: void aes_ctr_encrypt(const AES_KEY *key, uint8_t ctr[AES_BLOCK_SIZE], const uint8_t *in, size_t inlen, uint8_t *out);
functions.description: Encrypts or decrypts data using AES in CTR mode. Processes inlen bytes from in to out, XORing with the keystream generated from the evolving counter block. The ctr buffer is updated as counters advance.
requirements: key must have been initialized for encryption via aes_set_encrypt_key (CTR uses the encryption primitive for both directions)
ctr must point to AES_BLOCK_SIZE (16) bytes containing the initial counter block; it will be updated in place
in must point to inlen bytes of input; inlen may be zero
out must point to at least inlen bytes of writable memory
Because CTR is a stream mode, in and out may be the same buffer for in-place operation (not explicitly stated; behavior if aliased is unknown)

functions.name: aes_ctr_decrypt
functions.signature: void aes_ctr_decrypt(const AES_KEY *key, uint8_t ctr[AES_BLOCK_SIZE], const uint8_t *in, size_t inlen, uint8_t *out);
functions.description: Decrypts data using AES in CTR mode. Note: in this header, aes_ctr_decrypt is a macro alias of aes_ctr_encrypt, because CTR mode uses the same operation for encryption and decryption. Callers should pass the same parameters as aes_ctr_encrypt; the counter buffer is updated as the stream advances. There is no separate link-time symbol for aes_ctr_decrypt; it expands to a call to aes_ctr_encrypt.
requirements: key must point to a valid AES_KEY initialized for use (in CTR mode the encrypt key schedule is typically used; the header does not state which initializer, but the underlying function is aes_ctr_encrypt)
ctr must point to a buffer of exactly AES_BLOCK_SIZE (16) bytes; it is non-const and may be updated in place by the function
in must point to at least inlen bytes of input; inlen may be zero
out must point to a buffer with capacity of at least inlen bytes
this is provided as a macro; there is no separate function symbol at link time, it expands to aes_ctr_encrypt

functions.name: aes_gcm_encrypt
functions.signature: int aes_gcm_encrypt(const AES_KEY *key, const uint8_t *iv, size_t ivlen, const uint8_t *aad, size_t aadlen, const uint8_t *in, size_t inlen, uint8_t *out, size_t taglen, uint8_t *tag);
functions.description: Encrypts data using AES-GCM. Generates ciphertext from plaintext and computes an authentication tag over the AAD and ciphertext. The IV length is flexible; the tag length is caller-specified up to 16 bytes.
requirements: key must have been initialized for encryption via aes_set_encrypt_key
iv must point to ivlen bytes; ivlen must satisfy AES_GCM_IV_MIN_SIZE <= ivlen <= AES_GCM_IV_MAX_SIZE
aad may be NULL if aadlen is zero; otherwise must point to aadlen bytes; allowed range is AES_GCM_MIN_AAD_SIZE..AES_GCM_MAX_AAD_SIZE
in must point to inlen bytes; allowed range is AES_GCM_MIN_PLAINTEXT_SIZE..AES_GCM_MAX_PLAINTEXT_SIZE
out must point to at least inlen bytes of writable memory (ciphertext is same length as plaintext)
tag must point to at least taglen bytes of writable memory; taglen must be <= AES_GCM_MAX_TAG_SIZE (16). Minimum acceptable tag length is not specified (unknown)
The function returns an int; exact success/failure convention is unknown (not specified in header)

functions.name: aes_gcm_decrypt
functions.signature: int aes_gcm_decrypt(const AES_KEY *key, const uint8_t *iv, size_t ivlen, const uint8_t *aad, size_t aadlen, const uint8_t *in, size_t inlen, const uint8_t *tag, size_t taglen, uint8_t *out);
functions.description: Decrypts data using AES-GCM and verifies the authentication tag over the AAD and ciphertext. On successful verification, writes the plaintext to out.
requirements: key must have been initialized for encryption via aes_set_encrypt_key (GCM uses the encryption primitive)
iv must point to ivlen bytes; ivlen must satisfy AES_GCM_IV_MIN_SIZE <= ivlen <= AES_GCM_IV_MAX_SIZE
aad may be NULL if aadlen is zero; otherwise must point to aadlen bytes; allowed range is AES_GCM_MIN_AAD_SIZE..AES_GCM_MAX_AAD_SIZE
in must point to inlen bytes; allowed range is AES_GCM_MIN_PLAINTEXT_SIZE..AES_GCM_MAX_PLAINTEXT_SIZE
out must point to at least inlen bytes of writable memory
tag must point to at least taglen bytes; taglen must be <= AES_GCM_MAX_TAG_SIZE (16). Minimum acceptable tag length is not specified (unknown)
The function returns an int indicating authentication success/failure; exact convention is unknown (not specified in header)

functions.name: chacha20_init
functions.signature: void chacha20_init(CHACHA20_STATE *state, const uint8_t key[CHACHA20_KEY_SIZE], const uint8_t nonce[CHACHA20_NONCE_SIZE], uint32_t counter);
functions.description: Initializes a ChaCha20 stream cipher state with a 256-bit key, a 96-bit nonce, and a 32-bit initial block counter. Call this before generating any keystream. The state is prepared for subsequent keystream generation calls and encapsulates the internal block function state. Typical usage: allocate a CHACHA20_STATE, call chacha20_init with the key/nonce/counter, then call chacha20_generate_keystream to produce keystream bytes for XOR with plaintext/ciphertext. Nonce uniqueness per key is critical for security; the counter sets the starting block index.
requirements: state must be a valid, non-null pointer to a CHACHA20_STATE storage writable by the function.
key must be a non-null pointer to exactly CHACHA20_KEY_SIZE (32) bytes.
nonce must be a non-null pointer to exactly CHACHA20_NONCE_SIZE (12) bytes.
counter is a 32-bit initial block counter; valid range is 0..UINT32_MAX (no further constraints stated).
The function must be called before chacha20_generate_keystream to properly initialize the state.
Security requirement (inferred from ChaCha20 usage): do not reuse the same (key, nonce) pair; nonce must be unique for a given key to avoid keystream reuse.

functions.name: chacha20_generate_keystream
functions.signature: void chacha20_generate_keystream(CHACHA20_STATE *state, size_t counts, uint8_t *out);
functions.description: Generates ChaCha20 keystream from an initialized state into the provided output buffer. Intended to be called after chacha20_init; advances the internal state as keystream is produced. The meaning of counts (bytes vs. blocks) is not specified in this header and should be confirmed with the implementation or documentation; the output length requirement depends on that interpretation.
requirements: state must be a valid, non-null pointer to a CHACHA20_STATE previously initialized by chacha20_init.
out must be a non-null pointer to a writable buffer large enough to hold the generated keystream corresponding to counts (the exact mapping of counts to bytes is unspecified here).
The function may update/advance the internal state (inferred from stream cipher design); repeated calls will continue from the current position.
counts must be within a size_t range acceptable to the implementation; exact maximum not specified.
Caller must ensure correct interpretation of counts (bytes vs 64-byte blocks) per the library’s implementation to avoid buffer overflows or truncated output (unspecified in this header).

functions.name: gf128_set_zero
functions.signature: void gf128_set_zero(gf128_t r);
functions.description: Sets the GF(2^128) element r to the additive identity (zero). Intended to initialize or clear a field element before use. Internal representation is two uint64_t limbs; exact bit/endianness layout is library-defined and not documented here.
requirements: r must be a valid, writable pointer to gf128_t (i.e., storage for two uint64_t).
Aliasing with other objects is not applicable (single output argument).
Thread-safety of concurrent use on the same r is not guaranteed; callers must provide synchronization if r is shared.

functions.name: gf128_set_one
functions.signature: void gf128_set_one(gf128_t r);
functions.description: Sets the GF(2^128) element r to the multiplicative identity (one). Useful for initialization prior to multiplication or exponentiation. Field is defined by the irreducible polynomial x^128 + x^7 + x^2 + x + 1; the internal bit placement of 1 is library-defined and not documented here.
requirements: r must be a valid, writable pointer to gf128_t (two uint64_t).
Thread-safety of concurrent use on the same r is not guaranteed; callers must synchronize if r is shared.

functions.name: gf128_add

functions.description: Computes r = a + b in GF(2^128). Over GF(2), addition corresponds to bitwise XOR of the element representations. Intended for combining two field elements. The field is defined by x^128 + x^7 + x^2 + x + 1; reduction specifics are implicit in the implementation.
requirements: r must be a valid, writable gf128_t.
a and b must be valid, initialized gf128_t inputs.
Aliasing behavior is not documented; to be safe, avoid overlapping r with a or b unless the implementation is known to support in-place operation.
Callers must ensure a and b contain valid field elements as produced by this API (e.g., via set, from_bytes, from_hex, or prior operations).

functions.signature: void gf128_mul(gf128_t r, const gf128_t a, const gf128_t b);
functions.description: Computes r = a × b in GF(2^128) with reduction modulo the polynomial x^128 + x^7 + x^2 + x + 1. Use for finite-field multiplication as in GCM-like operations. Performance and constant-timeness are unspecified here.
requirements: r must be a valid, writable gf128_t.
a and b must be valid, initialized gf128_t inputs.
Aliasing behavior is not documented; avoid overlapping r with a or b to prevent undefined results.

functions.name: gf128_mul_by_2

functions.description: Computes r = a × 2 in GF(2^128), i.e., multiplication by the element {02} under the field defined by x^128 + x^7 + x^2 + x + 1. Useful for doubling operations common in GHASH/GCM implementations.
requirements: r must be a valid, writable gf128_t.
a must be a valid, initialized gf128_t input.
Aliasing behavior is not documented; avoid overlapping r with a unless confirmed safe.

functions.name: gf128_from_bytes

If clen > 0, c must point to a buffer of at least clen bytes.
aadlen and clen are sizes in bytes.

No state is retained; this function computes the complete GHASH in one call.

functions.name: ghash_init
