requirements: ctx must be a valid, writable GHASH_CTX pointer provided by the caller.
h must reference exactly 16 bytes containing the GHASH subkey (ENC_k(0^128)).
If aadlen > 0, aad must point to a buffer of at least aadlen bytes.
aadlen is in bytes.
Must be called before ghash_update and ghash_finish on the same ctx.
Function does not return a status; invalid inputs lead to undefined behavior.

functions.name: ghash_update
functions.signature: void ghash_update(GHASH_CTX *ctx, const uint8_t *c, size_t clen);
functions.description: Feeds additional data c of length clen into an initialized GHASH_CTX for incremental GHASH computation. Typically used to process ciphertext/plaintext data after associated data was handled in ghash_init. Use ghash_finish to finalize and get the 16-byte result.
requirements: ctx must have been initialized by a prior successful ghash_init call.
If clen > 0, c must point to a buffer of at least clen bytes.
clen is in bytes.
May be called zero or more times between ghash_init and ghash_finish; exact usage constraints beyond this are not documented in the header.
Function does not return a status; invalid inputs or calling without prior init lead to undefined behavior.

functions.name: ghash_finish
functions.signature: void ghash_finish(GHASH_CTX *ctx, uint8_t out[16]);
functions.description: Finalizes the incremental GHASH computation stored in ctx and writes the 16-byte authentication value to out. Must be called after ghash_init (and any ghash_update calls).
requirements: ctx must have been initialized by ghash_init and used only with compatible ghash_update calls.
out must reference a writable buffer of at least 16 bytes.
After finalization, the context contents may be altered; re-initialize with ghash_init before reuse (exact reuse guarantees are not documented).
Function does not return a status; invalid inputs or calling out of order lead to undefined behavior.

functions.name: BLOCK_CIPHER_sm4
functions.signature: const BLOCK_CIPHER *BLOCK_CIPHER_sm4(void);
functions.description: Returns a descriptor for the SM4 block cipher. Intended to be used with the generic block cipher APIs in this header to set keys and encrypt/decrypt single blocks.
requirements: No arguments required.
Callers should treat the returned pointer as a read-only, long-lived descriptor (do not modify or free).
The returned pointer may be used with block_cipher_set_encrypt_key/block_cipher_set_decrypt_key and subsequent block_cipher_encrypt/block_cipher_decrypt calls.
If the implementation fails to provide SM4 at runtime, the function could return NULL; callers should check for NULL before use (exact behavior not documented here).

functions.name: BLOCK_CIPHER_aes128
functions.signature: const BLOCK_CIPHER *BLOCK_CIPHER_aes128(void);
functions.description: Returns a descriptor for the AES-128 block cipher. Use with the generic block cipher APIs to set keys and encrypt/decrypt single blocks. Availability is conditional on the library being built with ENABLE_AES.
requirements: Only available when the library is compiled with ENABLE_AES defined; otherwise this symbol may be unavailable.
No arguments required.
Callers should treat the returned pointer as a read-only, long-lived descriptor (do not modify or free).
Use the returned descriptor with block_cipher_set_encrypt_key/block_cipher_set_decrypt_key and subsequent block_cipher_encrypt/block_cipher_decrypt calls.
If AES-128 is not supported at runtime, the function could return NULL; callers should check for NULL before use (exact behavior not documented here).

functions.name: block_cipher_from_name
functions.signature: const BLOCK_CIPHER *block_cipher_from_name(const char *name);
functions.description: Looks up a block cipher descriptor by name and returns a pointer to the corresponding BLOCK_CIPHER descriptor for use with the generic APIs.
requirements: name must be a valid, null-terminated C string.
Name matching and accepted aliases are not documented here; callers should use names recognized by this library (e.g., likely "SM4", and if built with AES enabled, possibly "AES-128").
Returns a const descriptor pointer or possibly NULL if the name is unrecognized; callers should check for NULL before use.
Do not modify or free the returned descriptor.

functions.name: block_cipher_name
functions.signature: const char *block_cipher_name(const BLOCK_CIPHER *cipher);
functions.description: Returns the human-readable name string for a given BLOCK_CIPHER descriptor.
requirements: cipher must be a valid, non-NULL pointer previously obtained (e.g., from BLOCK_CIPHER_sm4, BLOCK_CIPHER_aes128, or block_cipher_from_name).
The returned pointer points to immutable storage; do not modify or free it.
If cipher is invalid, the behavior or return value is not documented here; callers should handle a potential NULL return.

functions.name: block_cipher_set_encrypt_key
functions.signature: int block_cipher_set_encrypt_key(BLOCK_CIPHER_KEY *key, const BLOCK_CIPHER *cipher, const uint8_t *raw_key);
functions.description: Initializes a BLOCK_CIPHER_KEY for encryption using the specified cipher and raw key bytes. After a successful call, the key can be used with block_cipher_encrypt to process single blocks.
requirements: key must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to writable storage.
cipher must be a valid, non-NULL BLOCK_CIPHER descriptor matching the intended algorithm.
raw_key must point to at least cipher->key_size bytes containing the secret key material; exact length depends on the cipher (e.g., SM4: 16 bytes; AES-128: 16 bytes).
Must be called before block_cipher_encrypt with the same key instance.
Return value is an int; exact success/error convention is not specified in this header. Callers should check the return value and handle failures appropriately (e.g., treat non-success as an error).

functions.name: block_cipher_set_decrypt_key
functions.signature: int block_cipher_set_decrypt_key(BLOCK_CIPHER_KEY *key, const BLOCK_CIPHER *cipher, const uint8_t *raw_key);
functions.description: Initializes a BLOCK_CIPHER_KEY for decryption using the specified cipher and raw key bytes. After a successful call, the key can be used with block_cipher_decrypt to process single blocks.
requirements: key must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to writable storage.
cipher must be a valid, non-NULL BLOCK_CIPHER descriptor matching the intended algorithm.
raw_key must point to at least cipher->key_size bytes containing the secret key material; exact length depends on the cipher (e.g., SM4: 16 bytes; AES-128: 16 bytes).
Must be called before block_cipher_decrypt with the same key instance.
Return value is an int; exact success/error convention is not specified in this header. Callers should check the return value and handle failures appropriately (e.g., treat non-success as an error).

functions.name: block_cipher_encrypt
functions.signature: int block_cipher_encrypt(const BLOCK_CIPHER_KEY *key, const uint8_t *in, uint8_t *out);
functions.description: Encrypts a single block of plaintext using a previously initialized encryption key and writes the ciphertext block to out.
requirements: key must be a valid, non-NULL pointer initialized for encryption via block_cipher_set_encrypt_key for the same cipher.
in must point to at least key->cipher->block_size bytes of input (typically 16 bytes).
out must point to a writable buffer of at least key->cipher->block_size bytes (typically 16 bytes).
Function operates on exactly one block; for multi-block or streaming modes, use a higher-level mode of operation (not provided here).
Return value is an int; exact success/error convention is not specified in this header. Callers should check the return value and handle failures appropriately.

functions.name: block_cipher_decrypt
functions.signature: int block_cipher_decrypt(const BLOCK_CIPHER_KEY *key, const uint8_t *in, uint8_t *out);
functions.description: Decrypts a single block of ciphertext using a previously initialized decryption key and writes the plaintext block to out.
requirements: key must be a valid, non-NULL pointer initialized for decryption via block_cipher_set_decrypt_key for the same cipher.
in must point to at least key->cipher->block_size bytes of input (typically 16 bytes).
out must point to a writable buffer of at least key->cipher->block_size bytes (typically 16 bytes).
Function operates on exactly one block; for multi-block or streaming modes, use a higher-level mode of operation (not provided here).
Return value is an int; exact success/error convention is not specified in this header. Callers should check the return value and handle failures appropriately.

functions.name: sm4_set_encrypt_key
functions.signature: void sm4_set_encrypt_key(SM4_KEY *key, const uint8_t raw_key[SM4_KEY_SIZE]);
functions.description: Initializes an SM4_KEY with the round keys for encryption from a 16-byte raw key. Call before any SM4 encryption that uses SM4_KEY.
requirements: key must be a valid, writable pointer to an SM4_KEY structure
raw_key must point to exactly SM4_KEY_SIZE (16) bytes of key material

functions.name: sm4_set_decrypt_key
functions.signature: void sm4_set_decrypt_key(SM4_KEY *key, const uint8_t raw_key[SM4_KEY_SIZE]);
functions.description: Initializes an SM4_KEY with the round keys for decryption from a 16-byte raw key. Call before any SM4 decryption that uses SM4_KEY in decryption mode.
requirements: key must be a valid, writable pointer to an SM4_KEY structure
raw_key must point to exactly SM4_KEY_SIZE (16) bytes of key material

functions.name: sm4_encrypt
functions.signature: void sm4_encrypt(const SM4_KEY *key, const uint8_t in[SM4_BLOCK_SIZE], uint8_t out[SM4_BLOCK_SIZE]);
functions.description: Encrypts one 16-byte block with SM4 using a prepared key. ECB single-block primitive.
requirements: key must point to a key initialized via sm4_set_encrypt_key
in must point to at least SM4_BLOCK_SIZE (16) bytes
out must point to at least SM4_BLOCK_SIZE (16) bytes

functions.name: sm4_encrypt_blocks
functions.signature: void sm4_encrypt_blocks(const SM4_KEY *key, const uint8_t *in, size_t nblocks, uint8_t *out);
functions.description: Encrypts nblocks consecutive 16-byte blocks in ECB mode using a prepared key.
requirements: key must point to a key initialized via sm4_set_encrypt_key
in must point to at least nblocks * 16 bytes (or be NULL if nblocks == 0)
out must point to at least nblocks * 16 bytes (or be NULL if nblocks == 0)

functions.name: sm4_cbc_encrypt_blocks
functions.signature: void sm4_cbc_encrypt_blocks(const SM4_KEY *key, uint8_t iv[SM4_BLOCK_SIZE], const uint8_t *in, size_t nblocks, uint8_t *out);
functions.description: Encrypts input in CBC mode for an integral number of 16-byte blocks. IV is updated to the last ciphertext block.
requirements: key must point to a key initialized via sm4_set_encrypt_key
iv must point to a 16-byte buffer and will be modified in-place
nblocks must be the number of full 16-byte blocks in input
in must point to at least nblocks * 16 bytes
out must point to at least nblocks * 16 bytes

functions.name: sm4_cbc_decrypt_blocks
functions.signature: void sm4_cbc_decrypt_blocks(const SM4_KEY *key, uint8_t iv[SM4_BLOCK_SIZE], const uint8_t *in, size_t nblocks, uint8_t *out);
functions.description: Decrypts input in CBC mode for an integral number of 16-byte blocks. IV is updated to the last ciphertext block.
requirements: key must point to a key initialized via sm4_set_decrypt_key
iv must point to a 16-byte buffer and will be modified in-place
nblocks must be the number of full 16-byte blocks in input
in must point to at least nblocks * 16 bytes
out must point to at least nblocks * 16 bytes

functions.name: sm4_ctr_encrypt_blocks
functions.signature: void sm4_ctr_encrypt_blocks(const SM4_KEY *key, uint8_t ctr[16], const uint8_t *in, size_t nblocks, uint8_t *out);
functions.description: Encrypts/decrypts nblocks blocks in CTR mode (counter is incremented per block). ctr is updated in-place.
requirements: key must point to a key initialized via sm4_set_encrypt_key
ctr must point to a 16-byte counter block and will be modified
in must point to at least nblocks * 16 bytes
out must point to at least nblocks * 16 bytes

functions.name: sm4_ctr32_encrypt_blocks
functions.signature: void sm4_ctr32_encrypt_blocks(const SM4_KEY *key, uint8_t ctr[16], const uint8_t *in, size_t nblocks, uint8_t *out);
functions.description: Encrypts/decrypts nblocks blocks in CTR mode with a 32-bit counter increment (standard CTR32 variant). ctr is updated in-place.
requirements: key must point to a key initialized via sm4_set_encrypt_key
ctr must point to a 16-byte counter block and will be modified
in must point to at least nblocks * 16 bytes
out must point to at least nblocks * 16 bytes

functions.name: sm4_cbc_padding_encrypt
functions.signature: int sm4_cbc_padding_encrypt(const SM4_KEY *key, const uint8_t iv[SM4_BLOCK_SIZE], const uint8_t *in, size_t inlen, uint8_t *out, size_t *outlen);
functions.description: Encrypts variable-length data in CBC mode with padding (PKCS#7-style implied). Produces ciphertext and returns total bytes via outlen.
requirements: key must point to a key initialized via sm4_set_encrypt_key
iv must point to exactly 16 bytes and is treated as read-only by this API
in must point to inlen bytes (or be NULL if inlen == 0)
out must point to a buffer large enough to hold inlen + 16 bytes (for padding)
outlen must be a valid pointer for receiving the number of output bytes
return value indicates success (nonzero) or failure (zero); caller must check

functions.name: sm4_cbc_padding_decrypt
functions.signature: int sm4_cbc_padding_decrypt(const SM4_KEY *key, const uint8_t iv[SM4_BLOCK_SIZE], const uint8_t *in, size_t inlen, uint8_t *out, size_t *outlen);
functions.description: Decrypts variable-length data in CBC mode and removes padding. Validates padding and writes plaintext to out, length to outlen.
requirements: key must point to a key initialized via sm4_set_decrypt_key
iv must point to exactly 16 bytes and is treated as read-only by this API
in must point to inlen bytes and inlen must be a multiple of 16 (CBC ciphertext)
out must point to a buffer at least inlen bytes (plaintext will be <= inlen)
outlen must be a valid pointer for receiving the number of output bytes
return value indicates success (nonzero) or failure (zero); caller must check

functions.name: sm4_ctr_encrypt
functions.signature: void sm4_ctr_encrypt(const SM4_KEY *key, uint8_t ctr[16], const uint8_t *in, size_t inlen, uint8_t *out);
functions.description: Encrypts/decrypts arbitrary-length data in CTR mode. Counter block is updated in-place across the stream.
requirements: key must point to a key initialized via sm4_set_encrypt_key
ctr must point to a 16-byte counter and will be modified
in must point to at least inlen bytes (or be NULL if inlen == 0)
out must point to at least inlen bytes

functions.name: sm4_ctr32_encrypt
functions.signature: void sm4_ctr32_encrypt(const SM4_KEY *key, uint8_t ctr[16], const uint8_t *in, size_t inlen, uint8_t *out);
functions.description: Encrypts/decrypts arbitrary-length data in CTR mode with 32-bit counter increment semantics. Counter is updated in-place.
requirements: key must point to a key initialized via sm4_set_encrypt_key
ctr must point to a 16-byte counter and will be modified
in must point to at least inlen bytes (or be NULL if inlen == 0)
out must point to at least inlen bytes

functions.name: sm4_cbc_encrypt_init
functions.signature: int sm4_cbc_encrypt_init(SM4_CBC_CTX *ctx, const uint8_t key[SM4_KEY_SIZE], const uint8_t iv[SM4_BLOCK_SIZE]);
functions.description: Initializes a CBC encryption context with a 16-byte key and 16-byte IV for streaming-style API.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, writable pointer
key must point to exactly 16 bytes
iv must point to exactly 16 bytes
return value indicates success (nonzero) or failure (zero); caller must check

functions.name: sm4_cbc_encrypt_update
functions.signature: int sm4_cbc_encrypt_update(SM4_CBC_CTX *ctx, const uint8_t *in, size_t inlen, uint8_t *out, size_t *outlen);
functions.description: Feeds plaintext to the CBC encryption context and emits ciphertext. May buffer partial blocks; outlen reports produced bytes.
requirements: ctx must be initialized via sm4_cbc_encrypt_init
in must point to at least inlen bytes (or be NULL if inlen == 0)
out must point to sufficient space for produced ciphertext (>= inlen + up to block-1)
outlen must be a valid pointer to receive output length
return value indicates success (nonzero) or failure (zero); caller must check

functions.name: sm4_cbc_encrypt_finish
functions.signature: int sm4_cbc_encrypt_finish(SM4_CBC_CTX *ctx, uint8_t *out, size_t *outlen);
functions.description: Finalizes CBC encryption, applying padding and emitting any remaining ciphertext.
requirements: ctx must be initialized via sm4_cbc_encrypt_init and used with update
out must have room for up to one full block (16 bytes) of final output
outlen must be a valid pointer to receive output length
return value indicates success (nonzero) or failure (zero); caller must check

functions.name: sm4_cbc_decrypt_init
functions.signature: int sm4_cbc_decrypt_init(SM4_CBC_CTX *ctx, const uint8_t key[SM4_KEY_SIZE], const uint8_t iv[SM4_BLOCK_SIZE]);
functions.description: Initializes a CBC decryption context with a 16-byte key and 16-byte IV for streaming-style API.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, writable pointer
key must point to exactly 16 bytes
iv must point to exactly 16 bytes
return value indicates success (nonzero) or failure (zero); caller must check

functions.name: sm4_cbc_decrypt_update
functions.signature: int sm4_cbc_decrypt_update(SM4_CBC_CTX *ctx, const uint8_t *in, size_t inlen, uint8_t *out, size_t *outlen);
functions.description: Feeds ciphertext to the CBC decryption context and emits plaintext. May buffer until full blocks are available.
requirements: ctx must be initialized via sm4_cbc_decrypt_init
in must point to at least inlen bytes and should be in full blocks except possibly final
out must point to sufficient space for produced plaintext
outlen must be a valid pointer to receive output length
return value indicates success (nonzero) or failure (zero); caller must check

functions.name: sm4_cbc_decrypt_finish
functions.signature: int sm4_cbc_decrypt_finish(SM4_CBC_CTX *ctx, uint8_t *out, size_t *outlen);
functions.description: Finalizes CBC decryption, validates and removes padding, and emits any remaining plaintext.
requirements: ctx must be initialized via sm4_cbc_decrypt_init and used with update
out must have room for up to one block (16 bytes) of final output
outlen must be a valid pointer to receive output length
return value indicates success (nonzero) or failure (zero); caller must check

functions.name: sm4_ctr_encrypt_init
functions.signature: int sm4_ctr_encrypt_init(SM4_CTR_CTX *ctx, const uint8_t key[SM4_KEY_SIZE], const uint8_t ctr[SM4_BLOCK_SIZE]);
functions.description: Initializes a CTR streaming context with a 16-byte key and initial counter block.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, writable pointer
key must point to exactly 16 bytes
ctr must point to exactly 16 bytes
return value indicates success (nonzero) or failure (zero); caller must check

functions.name: sm4_ctr_encrypt_update
functions.signature: int sm4_ctr_encrypt_update(SM4_CTR_CTX *ctx, const uint8_t *in, size_t inlen, uint8_t *out, size_t *outlen);
functions.description: Feeds data through the CTR context, producing keystream XOR output. Symmetric for encryption/decryption.
requirements: ctx must be initialized via sm4_ctr_encrypt_init
in must point to at least inlen bytes (or be NULL if inlen == 0)
out must point to at least inlen bytes (produced bytes)
outlen must be a valid pointer to receive output length
return value indicates success (nonzero) or failure (zero); caller must check

functions.name: sm4_ctr_encrypt_finish
functions.signature: int sm4_ctr_encrypt_finish(SM4_CTR_CTX *ctx, uint8_t *out, size_t *outlen);
functions.description: Finalizes CTR streaming operation, emitting any buffered bytes (if any).
requirements: ctx must be initialized via sm4_ctr_encrypt_init and used with update
out may be non-NULL if final bytes are produced; ensure sufficient space
outlen must be a valid pointer to receive final output length (possibly zero)
return value indicates success (nonzero) or failure (zero); caller must check

functions.name: sm4_ctr32_encrypt_init
functions.signature: int sm4_ctr32_encrypt_init(SM4_CTR_CTX *ctx, const uint8_t key[SM4_KEY_SIZE], const uint8_t ctr[SM4_BLOCK_SIZE]);
functions.description: Initializes a CTR32 streaming context with a 16-byte key and initial counter block (32-bit counter semantics).
requirements: ctx must be a valid, writable pointer
key must point to exactly 16 bytes
ctr must point to exactly 16 bytes
return value indicates success (nonzero) or failure (zero); caller must check

functions.name: sm4_ctr32_encrypt_update
functions.signature: int sm4_ctr32_encrypt_update(SM4_CTR_CTX *ctx, const uint8_t *in, size_t inlen, uint8_t *out, size_t *outlen);
functions.description: Feeds data through the CTR32 context, producing keystream XOR output. Symmetric for encryption/decryption.
requirements: ctx must be initialized via sm4_ctr32_encrypt_init
in must point to at least inlen bytes (or be NULL if inlen == 0)
out must point to at least inlen bytes (produced bytes)
outlen must be a valid pointer to receive output length
return value indicates success (nonzero) or failure (zero); caller must check

functions.name: sm4_ctr32_encrypt_finish
functions.signature: int sm4_ctr32_encrypt_finish(SM4_CTR_CTX *ctx, uint8_t *out, size_t *outlen);
functions.description: Finalizes CTR32 streaming operation, emitting any buffered bytes (if any).
requirements: ctx must be initialized via sm4_ctr32_encrypt_init and used with update
out may be non-NULL if final bytes are produced; ensure sufficient space
outlen must be a valid pointer to receive final output length (possibly zero)
return value indicates success (nonzero) or failure (zero); caller must check

functions.name: sm4_gcm_encrypt
functions.signature: int sm4_gcm_encrypt(const SM4_KEY *key, const uint8_t *iv, size_t ivlen, const uint8_t *aad, size_t aadlen, const uint8_t *in, size_t inlen, uint8_t *out, size_t taglen, uint8_t *tag);
functions.description: All-in-one SM4-GCM authenticated encryption: encrypts plaintext, authenticates AAD and ciphertext, and outputs a tag.
requirements: key must point to a key initialized via sm4_set_encrypt_key
iv must point to ivlen bytes; ivlen must satisfy SM4_GCM_MIN_IV_SIZE..SM4_GCM_MAX_IV_SIZE (default 12)
aad may be NULL if aadlen==0; aadlen must be within SM4_GCM_MIN_AAD_SIZE..SM4_GCM_MAX_AAD_SIZE
in/inlen define plaintext; inlen must be within SM4_GCM_MIN_PLAINTEXT_SIZE..SM4_GCM_MAX_PLAINTEXT_SIZE
out must point to at least inlen bytes
taglen must be within SM4_GCM_MIN_TAG_SIZE..SM4_GCM_MAX_TAG_SIZE (default 16)
tag must point to at least taglen bytes
return value indicates success (nonzero) or failure (zero); caller must check

functions.name: sm4_gcm_decrypt
functions.signature: int sm4_gcm_decrypt(const SM4_KEY *key, const uint8_t *iv, size_t ivlen, const uint8_t *aad, size_t aadlen, const uint8_t *in, size_t inlen, const uint8_t *tag, size_t taglen, uint8_t *out);
functions.description: All-in-one SM4-GCM authenticated decryption: verifies tag over AAD and ciphertext, and on success outputs plaintext.
requirements: key must point to a key initialized via sm4_set_encrypt_key (GCM uses encryption primitive)
iv must point to ivlen bytes; ivlen must satisfy SM4_GCM_MIN_IV_SIZE..SM4_GCM_MAX_IV_SIZE
aad may be NULL if aadlen==0; aadlen must be within SM4_GCM_MIN_AAD_SIZE..SM4_GCM_MAX_AAD_SIZE
in/inlen define ciphertext; inlen must be within SM4_GCM_MIN_PLAINTEXT_SIZE..SM4_GCM_MAX_PLAINTEXT_SIZE
out must point to at least inlen bytes
tag must point to at least taglen bytes; taglen must be within SM4_GCM_MIN_TAG_SIZE..SM4_GCM_MAX_TAG_SIZE
return value indicates success (nonzero) or failure (zero); caller must check and treat failure as authentication failure

functions.name: sm4_gcm_encrypt_init
functions.signature: int sm4_gcm_encrypt_init(SM4_GCM_CTX *ctx, const uint8_t *key, size_t keylen, const uint8_t *iv, size_t ivlen, const uint8_t *aad, size_t aadlen, size_t taglen);
functions.description: Initializes a streaming SM4-GCM encryption context with key/IV/AAD and requested tag length.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, writable pointer
key must point to keylen bytes; keylen must be 16 (SM4)
iv must point to ivlen bytes; ivlen within SM4_GCM_MIN_IV_SIZE..SM4_GCM_MAX_IV_SIZE
aad may be NULL if aadlen==0; aadlen within SM4_GCM_MIN_AAD_SIZE..SM4_GCM_MAX_AAD_SIZE
taglen within SM4_GCM_MIN_TAG_SIZE..SM4_GCM_MAX_TAG_SIZE
return value indicates success (nonzero) or failure (zero); caller must check

functions.name: sm4_gcm_encrypt_update
functions.signature: int sm4_gcm_encrypt_update(SM4_GCM_CTX *ctx, const uint8_t *in, size_t inlen, uint8_t *out, size_t *outlen);

requirements: ctx must be initialized via sm4_gcm_encrypt_init
in must point to at least inlen bytes (or be NULL if inlen == 0)
out must point to at least inlen bytes
outlen must be a valid pointer to receive number of bytes output
return value indicates success (nonzero) or failure (zero); caller must check

functions.name: sm4_gcm_encrypt_finish
functions.signature: int sm4_gcm_encrypt_finish(SM4_GCM_CTX *ctx, uint8_t *out, size_t *outlen);
functions.description: Finalizes GCM encryption, producing the authentication tag internally (retrieved according to the implementation) and any final bytes.
requirements: ctx must be initialized and used via sm4_gcm_encrypt_init/update
out may be non-NULL if final bytes are produced; ensure sufficient space
outlen must be a valid pointer to receive final output length (possibly zero)
return value indicates success (nonzero) or failure (zero); caller must check

functions.name: sm4_gcm_decrypt_init
functions.signature: int sm4_gcm_decrypt_init(SM4_GCM_CTX *ctx, const uint8_t *key, size_t keylen, const uint8_t *iv, size_t ivlen, const uint8_t *aad, size_t aadlen, size_t taglen);
functions.description: Initializes a streaming SM4-GCM decryption context with key/IV/AAD and expected tag length.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, writable pointer
key must point to keylen bytes; keylen must be 16 (SM4)
iv must point to ivlen bytes; ivlen within SM4_GCM_MIN_IV_SIZE..SM4_GCM_MAX_IV_SIZE
aad may be NULL if aadlen==0; aadlen within SM4_GCM_MIN_AAD_SIZE..SM4_GCM_MAX_AAD_SIZE
taglen within SM4_GCM_MIN_TAG_SIZE..SM4_GCM_MAX_TAG_SIZE
return value indicates success (nonzero) or failure (zero); caller must check

functions.name: sm4_gcm_decrypt_update
functions.signature: int sm4_gcm_decrypt_update(SM4_GCM_CTX *ctx, const uint8_t *in, size_t inlen, uint8_t *out, size_t *outlen);
functions.description: Processes ciphertext through the GCM decryption context, emitting plaintext while accumulating authentication state.
requirements: ctx must be initialized via sm4_gcm_decrypt_init
in must point to at least inlen bytes (or be NULL if inlen == 0)
out must point to at least inlen bytes
outlen must be a valid pointer to receive number of bytes output

requirements: ctx must have been successfully initialized and used only with sm4_cbc_sm3_hmac_decrypt_update prior to this call.
out must be a valid writable buffer with sufficient space for any remaining plaintext (exact size not documented).
outlen must be a valid pointer to size_t to receive the number of bytes written.
If authentication fails, callers should expect a failure return and no plaintext output; exact error signaling is not documented.
After finish returns, the context should not be reused for more decrypt_update calls without reinitialization.

functions.name: sm4_cl_set_encrypt_key
functions.signature: int sm4_cl_set_encrypt_key(SM4_CL_CTX *ctx, const uint8_t key[16]);
functions.description: Initializes the SM4_CL_CTX with the round keys and any required OpenCL state for SM4 encryption using the provided 16-byte key. Typical usage: allocate/zero an SM4_CL_CTX, call this function once with a 16-byte key, then use the context with encryption operations (e.g., CTR mode). Returns 1 on success or 0/negative on failure (exact conventions unknown).
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an SM4_CL_CTX instance.
key must point to exactly 16 bytes (128-bit SM4 key).
The context must not be used for encryption operations until this function returns success.
If the function fails (non-success return), the context should not be used for encryption (exact recovery/cleanup steps unknown).
Thread-safety and reentrancy are unspecified; avoid concurrent mutation of the same ctx from multiple threads.

functions.name: sm4_cl_set_decrypt_key
functions.signature: int sm4_cl_set_decrypt_key(SM4_CL_CTX *ctx, const uint8_t key[16]);
functions.description: Initializes the SM4_CL_CTX with the round keys and any required OpenCL state for SM4 decryption using the provided 16-byte key. Intended for modes or operations that use the decryption key schedule. Returns 1 on success or 0/negative on failure (exact conventions unknown).
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an SM4_CL_CTX instance.
key must point to exactly 16 bytes (128-bit SM4 key).
The context must not be used for decryption operations until this function returns success.
If the function fails (non-success return), the context should not be used for decryption (exact recovery/cleanup steps unknown).
Thread-safety and reentrancy are unspecified; avoid concurrent mutation of the same ctx from multiple threads.

functions.name: sm4_cl_ctr32_encrypt_blocks
functions.signature: int sm4_cl_ctr32_encrypt_blocks(SM4_CL_CTX *ctx, uint8_t iv[16], const uint8_t *in, size_t nblocks, uint8_t *out);
functions.description: Encrypts nblocks of data using SM4 in CTR mode with a 128-bit IV/counter, processing full 16-byte blocks on an OpenCL device using the provided SM4_CL_CTX. The 32-bit counter is typically encoded in the last 4 bytes of iv and incremented per block (exact layout unspecified). On success, writes nblocks*16 bytes to out and updates the IV/counter in-place if the implementation does so (behavior unspecified). Return code conventions are not documented.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an SM4_CL_CTX that has been initialized for encryption (typically via sm4_cl_set_encrypt_key).
iv must point to a 16-byte buffer; it represents the initial counter block. The exact counter field placement/endianness is unspecified.
in must point to at least nblocks*16 bytes of input; out must point to at least nblocks*16 bytes of writable output.
nblocks specifies the number of complete 16-byte blocks to process; if nblocks is 0, no data is processed.
in and out must be valid for the specified size and may alias behavior is unspecified; use distinct buffers to be safe.
This function operates on full blocks only; partial blocks are not supported by this API.
Return value semantics (success/failure codes) are not documented; callers should check for a non-success value and handle errors accordingly.
Thread-safety with respect to the same ctx or buffers is unspecified; do not call concurrently on the same ctx or overlapping buffers.

functions.name: sm4_cl_cleanup
functions.signature: void sm4_cl_cleanup(SM4_CL_CTX *ctx);
functions.description: Releases and clears resources associated with an SM4_CL_CTX, including OpenCL objects and key material. After cleanup, the context should be considered invalid until reinitialized. Safe behavior when called on an uninitialized or partially initialized context is not documented.
requirements: ctx must be a valid pointer to an SM4_CL_CTX (may be NULL if caller guards calls; NULL handling is unspecified).
Do not use the ctx for any further cryptographic operations after this call unless it is reinitialized.
If other threads might use ctx, ensure they have finished before cleanup (concurrency guarantees are unspecified).

functions.name: sm4_ctr_sm3_hmac_encrypt_init
functions.signature: int sm4_ctr_sm3_hmac_encrypt_init(SM4_CTR_SM3_HMAC_CTX *ctx, const uint8_t key[48], const uint8_t iv[16], const uint8_t *aad, size_t aadlen);
functions.description: Initializes a streaming authenticated-encryption operation that uses SM4 in CTR mode for encryption and SM3-HMAC for authentication (Encrypt-then-MAC). The function sets up ctx with the provided 48-byte key (likely split between SM4 and HMAC), a 16-byte IV/nonce, and optional associated data (AAD) that is authenticated but not encrypted. After a successful init, call sm4_ctr_sm3_hmac_encrypt_update repeatedly to process plaintext to ciphertext, then sm4_ctr_sm3_hmac_encrypt_finish to finalize and output the authentication tag and any remaining data. Exact return-value semantics and tag size are not documented here; the SM3 HMAC tag is typically SM3_HMAC_SIZE bytes.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, writable pointer to an SM4_CTR_SM3_HMAC_CTX structure.
key must point to at least 48 bytes; the function expects exactly 48 bytes (SM4_CTR_SM3_HMAC_KEY_SIZE).
iv must point to at least 16 bytes; the function expects exactly 16 bytes (SM4_CTR_SM3_HMAC_IV_SIZE).
aad may be NULL only if aadlen is 0; if aadlen > 0, aad must point to at least aadlen bytes. (Inferred from common AAD usage.)
Must be called before any encrypt_update or encrypt_finish on the same ctx.
Do not mix encrypt_* and decrypt_* operations on the same ctx instance without reinitializing it.
The IV/nonce should be unique for each encryption under a given key to maintain security in CTR mode (inferred from CTR requirements).
This API does not expose a mechanism to supply AAD after initialization; all AAD for the message should be provided here.
Thread-safety is not implied; the same ctx must not be used concurrently from multiple threads.

functions.name: sm4_ctr_sm3_hmac_encrypt_update
functions.signature: int sm4_ctr_sm3_hmac_encrypt_update(SM4_CTR_SM3_HMAC_CTX *ctx, const uint8_t *in, size_t inlen, uint8_t *out, size_t *outlen);
functions.description: Encrypts a chunk of plaintext using SM4-CTR and updates the SM3-HMAC authenticator within the active encryption context. Call repeatedly to process streaming data after a successful encrypt_init. Typically produces ciphertext of the same length as input; the exact out length behavior is not documented here. Finalize with encrypt_finish to get the authentication tag and flush any remaining bytes.
requirements: ctx must have been successfully initialized by sm4_ctr_sm3_hmac_encrypt_init and not yet finalized.
in must point to at least inlen bytes; in may be NULL only if inlen is 0.
out must point to a writable buffer large enough to hold the produced ciphertext; in CTR mode this is typically at least inlen bytes (exact behavior unspecified here).
outlen must be a valid, writable pointer; on return it will receive the number of bytes written to out.
It is unspecified whether in-place operation (out overlapping in) is supported; if unsure, use distinct buffers or ensure safe overlap handling.
May be called zero or more times before encrypt_finish; order must be preserved.
Return-value success/failure convention is not specified here; callers should check for a nonzero/positive return per library convention.

functions.name: sm4_ctr_sm3_hmac_encrypt_finish
functions.signature: int sm4_ctr_sm3_hmac_encrypt_finish(SM4_CTR_SM3_HMAC_CTX *ctx, uint8_t *out, size_t *outlen);
functions.description: Finalizes the SM4-CTR + SM3-HMAC encryption operation. Produces any final output and the authentication tag for the message (tag size is typically SM3_HMAC_SIZE). After this call, the ctx should be considered finished and must be reinitialized before reuse.
requirements: ctx must be in an active encryption operation started by sm4_ctr_sm3_hmac_encrypt_init and not previously finalized.
out must point to a buffer large enough to receive any final bytes and the authentication tag; exact required size is not documented here, but the tag is typically SM3_HMAC_SIZE bytes.
outlen must be a valid, writable pointer; on return it will contain the number of bytes written to out.
No further encrypt_update calls may be made on ctx after a successful finish; reinitialize the context for a new message.
Return-value success/failure convention is not specified here; callers should check per library convention.

functions.name: sm4_ctr_sm3_hmac_decrypt_init
functions.signature: int sm4_ctr_sm3_hmac_decrypt_init(SM4_CTR_SM3_HMAC_CTX *ctx, const uint8_t key[48], const uint8_t iv[16], const uint8_t *aad, size_t aadlen);
functions.description: Initializes a streaming authenticated-decryption operation complementary to the encrypt path. Sets up ctx for SM4-CTR decryption with SM3-HMAC verification using the provided 48-byte key, 16-byte IV, and optional AAD. After init, feed ciphertext (and, per common design, the trailing authentication tag) via decrypt_update calls, then call decrypt_finish to finalize and verify the tag.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, writable pointer to an SM4_CTR_SM3_HMAC_CTX structure.
key must point to exactly 48 bytes (SM4_CTR_SM3_HMAC_KEY_SIZE).
iv must point to exactly 16 bytes (SM4_CTR_SM3_HMAC_IV_SIZE) and must match the IV used for encryption.
aad may be NULL only if aadlen is 0; if aadlen > 0, aad must point to at least aadlen bytes and must match the AAD used for encryption.
Must be called before any decrypt_update or decrypt_finish on the same ctx.
Do not mix encrypt_* and decrypt_* operations on the same ctx without reinitialization.
Thread-safety is not implied; the same ctx must not be used concurrently from multiple threads.

functions.name: sm4_ctr_sm3_hmac_decrypt_update
functions.signature: int sm4_ctr_sm3_hmac_decrypt_update(SM4_CTR_SM3_HMAC_CTX *ctx, const uint8_t *in, size_t inlen, uint8_t *out, size_t *outlen);
functions.description: Processes a chunk of input during authenticated decryption. Decrypts SM4-CTR ciphertext to plaintext and updates the SM3-HMAC verification state. Typically outputs plaintext of the same size as the ciphertext provided, except for any final tag bytes that may be processed at the end; exact behavior is not documented here.
requirements: ctx must have been successfully initialized by sm4_ctr_sm3_hmac_decrypt_init and not yet finalized.
in must point to at least inlen bytes; in may be NULL only if inlen is 0.
out must point to a writable buffer large enough to hold produced plaintext; typically at least inlen bytes (exact behavior unspecified).
outlen must be a valid, writable pointer; on return it will receive the number of bytes written to out.
It is unspecified whether in-place operation (out overlapping in) is supported; if unsure, use distinct buffers or ensure safe overlap handling.
May be called zero or more times before decrypt_finish; order must be preserved.
Return-value success/failure convention and behavior on authentication failure during streaming are not specified here; callers should check return values per library convention.

functions.name: sm4_ctr_sm3_hmac_decrypt_finish
functions.signature: int sm4_ctr_sm3_hmac_decrypt_finish(SM4_CTR_SM3_HMAC_CTX *ctx, uint8_t *out, size_t *outlen);
functions.description: Finalizes the authenticated decryption, completing SM3-HMAC verification and producing any remaining plaintext. If authentication fails (e.g., tag mismatch), this function is expected to report failure via its return value; exact semantics are not documented here. After this call, the ctx must be reinitialized before reuse.
requirements: ctx must be in an active decryption operation started by sm4_ctr_sm3_hmac_decrypt_init and not previously finalized.

If any final bytes are emitted, out must point to a buffer large enough; outlen must be a valid, writable pointer to receive the number of bytes written. Exact amount of final output is unspecified here.
All ciphertext and the authentication tag (typically SM3_HMAC_SIZE bytes) must have been supplied via decrypt_update before calling finish; the API does not take a separate tag parameter.

On authentication failure, the function likely indicates an error via its return value; callers must check the return code and discard any output if verification fails (behavior not explicitly documented here).
No further decrypt_update calls may be made on ctx after a successful finish; reinitialize the context for a new message.

functions.name: hmac_size
functions.signature: size_t hmac_size(const HMAC_CTX *ctx);
functions.description: Returns the length in bytes of the MAC produced by the HMAC context’s configured digest. Typical usage: call after a successful hmac_init to determine how many bytes to allocate for the output MAC.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an HMAC_CTX.
ctx should have been successfully initialized via hmac_init before calling hmac_size; behavior is otherwise unknown.
The returned size corresponds to the digest size associated with ctx’s digest implementation.

functions.name: hmac_init
functions.signature: int hmac_init(HMAC_CTX *ctx, const DIGEST *digest, const uint8_t *key, size_t keylen);
functions.description: Initializes an HMAC context to use the specified digest and key. Typical usage: call once to set up ctx before one or more hmac_update calls, followed by hmac_finish to obtain the MAC.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to writable HMAC_CTX storage.
digest must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a DIGEST implementation supported by the library.
key may be NULL only if keylen is 0; otherwise key must point to at least keylen bytes of readable memory.
keylen is the length of key in bytes.
Must be called before hmac_update and hmac_finish on the same ctx.
Return value convention (success/failure code) is not specified in this header and is therefore unknown.

functions.name: hmac_update
functions.signature: int hmac_update(HMAC_CTX *ctx, const uint8_t *data, size_t datalen);
functions.description: Feeds message data into an initialized HMAC context. Can be called multiple times to process a message in chunks prior to finalizing with hmac_finish.
requirements: ctx must be a valid HMAC_CTX previously initialized with hmac_init.
data may be NULL only if datalen is 0; otherwise it must point to at least datalen bytes of readable memory.
May be called multiple times between hmac_init and hmac_finish.
Return value convention (success/failure code) is not specified in this header and is therefore unknown.

functions.name: hmac_finish
functions.signature: int hmac_finish(HMAC_CTX *ctx, uint8_t *mac, size_t *maclen);
functions.description: Finalizes the HMAC computation for the provided context and writes the MAC to the output buffer. Also returns the length of the MAC via maclen. Typical usage: call once after all hmac_update calls.
requirements: ctx must be a valid HMAC_CTX that has been successfully initialized with hmac_init (and optionally updated with hmac_update).
mac must point to a writable buffer large enough to hold the MAC; allocate at least hmac_size(ctx) bytes (or HMAC_MAX_SIZE if uncertain).
maclen must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to size_t for receiving the number of bytes written.
After calling hmac_finish, the ctx may need reinitialization before reuse; exact reuse semantics are not specified and thus unknown.
Return value convention (success/failure code) is not specified in this header and is therefore unknown.

functions.name: hmac
functions.signature: int hmac(const DIGEST *md, const uint8_t *key, size_t keylen, const uint8_t *data, size_t dlen, uint8_t *mac, size_t *maclen);
functions.description: One-shot HMAC computation using the specified digest, key, and input data. Computes the MAC of data and writes the result to mac, returning the number of bytes written via maclen. Intended for single-buffer use without managing an HMAC_CTX.
requirements: md must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a DIGEST implementation supported by the library.
key may be NULL only if keylen is 0; otherwise key must point to at least keylen bytes of readable memory.
data may be NULL only if dlen is 0; otherwise it must point to at least dlen bytes of readable memory.
mac must point to a writable buffer large enough to hold the MAC; allocate at least the digest’s output size (or HMAC_MAX_SIZE if uncertain).
maclen must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to size_t for receiving the number of bytes written.
Return value convention (success/failure code) is not specified in this header and is therefore unknown.

functions.name: hkdf_extract
functions.signature: int hkdf_extract(const DIGEST *digest, const uint8_t *salt, size_t saltlen, const uint8_t *ikm, size_t ikmlen, uint8_t *prk, size_t *prklen);
functions.description: Computes the HKDF-Extract step (RFC 5869) using the specified hash/digest. It derives a pseudorandom key (PRK) from input keying material (IKM) and an optional salt, writing the PRK to prk and its length to prklen. Typical usage: call first to obtain a PRK, then pass that PRK to hkdf_expand.
requirements: digest must be a valid, initialized pointer to a supported DIGEST algorithm (e.g., SM3, SHA-256) and must remain valid for the call duration.
salt must point to at least saltlen bytes; behavior when saltlen == 0 and salt == NULL is unspecified by this header (commonly allowed by HKDF, but unknown here).
ikm must point to at least ikmlen bytes of input keying material.
prk must point to a writable buffer large enough to hold the digest output size for the chosen digest (i.e., HashLen bytes).
prklen must be a valid, writable pointer; on success it will be set to the number of bytes written (typically HashLen).
Return value is an int; specific success/failure codes are not documented here (unknown).

functions.name: hkdf_expand
functions.signature: int hkdf_expand(const DIGEST *digest, const uint8_t *prk, size_t prklen, const uint8_t *opt_info, size_t opt_infolen, size_t L, uint8_t *okm);
functions.description: Computes the HKDF-Expand step (RFC 5869) using the specified hash/digest. It expands a pseudorandom key (PRK) into L bytes of output keying material (OKM), optionally binding context/application-specific info.
requirements: digest must be a valid, initialized pointer to a supported DIGEST algorithm and must remain valid for the call duration.
prk must point to a PRK produced by hkdf_extract for the same digest algorithm.
prklen must equal the digest output size (HashLen) for the given digest (RFC 5869 requirement).
opt_info may be optional; when opt_infolen is 0, opt_info may be NULL (inferred by parameter name opt_info).
L is the number of bytes to output and must be <= 255 * HashLen (RFC 5869 limit).
okm must point to a writable buffer of at least L bytes.
Return value is an int; specific success/failure codes are not documented here (unknown).

functions.name: sm3_hkdf_extract
functions.signature: int sm3_hkdf_extract(const uint8_t *salt, size_t saltlen, const uint8_t *ikm, size_t ikmlen, uint8_t prk[32]);
functions.description: SM3-specific HKDF-Extract (RFC 5869) that derives a 32-byte pseudorandom key (PRK) from IKM and an optional salt using the SM3 hash. Use prior to sm3_hkdf_expand.
requirements: salt must point to at least saltlen bytes; behavior when saltlen == 0 and salt == NULL is unspecified by this header (unknown).
ikm must point to at least ikmlen bytes of input keying material.
prk must point to a writable buffer of at least 32 bytes; exactly 32 bytes will be written on success.
Return value is an int; specific success/failure codes are not documented here (unknown).

functions.name: sm3_hkdf_expand
functions.signature: int sm3_hkdf_expand(const uint8_t prk[32], const uint8_t *opt_info, size_t opt_infolen, size_t L, uint8_t *okm);
functions.description: SM3-specific HKDF-Expand (RFC 5869) that expands a 32-byte PRK into L bytes of output keying material (OKM), optionally binding context/application-specific info.
requirements: prk must point to a valid 32-byte PRK generated by sm3_hkdf_extract.
opt_info may be optional; when opt_infolen is 0, opt_info may be NULL (inferred by parameter name opt_info).
L must be <= 255 * 32 (8160) bytes per RFC 5869 for SM3.
okm must point to a writable buffer of at least L bytes.
Return value is an int; specific success/failure codes are not documented here (unknown).

functions.name: pbkdf2_genkey
functions.signature: int pbkdf2_genkey(const DIGEST *digest, const char *pass, size_t passlen, const uint8_t *salt, size_t saltlen, size_t iter, size_t outlen, uint8_t *out);
functions.description: Derives a key from a password using PBKDF2 with HMAC and the specified hash (DIGEST). Callers provide the password bytes, a salt, an iteration count, and an output buffer of the desired length. Typical usage is to generate cryptographic keys from user passwords; larger iteration counts increase computational cost. The specific DIGEST must be compatible with HMAC as provided by gmssl/hmac.h. Return value semantics are not documented here; consult the library for exact success/failure indicators.
requirements: digest must be a valid pointer to a supported DIGEST implementation usable with HMAC (from gmssl/hmac.h).
pass must point to at least passlen bytes (may be binary-safe); the pointer must be valid for reading passlen bytes.
salt must point to at least saltlen bytes; the pointer must be valid for reading saltlen bytes.
saltlen should not exceed PBKDF2_MAX_SALT_SIZE (64), inferred from the defined constant.
iter should be within [PBKDF2_MIN_ITER, PBKDF2_MAX_ITER] (10000..INT_MAX), inferred from the defined constants.
out must point to a writable buffer of at least outlen bytes; the buffer will be filled with the derived key.
The function performs PBKDF2 key derivation; outlen determines the length of the derived key to generate.

functions.name: pbkdf2_hmac_sm3_genkey
functions.signature: int pbkdf2_hmac_sm3_genkey(const char *pass, size_t passlen, const uint8_t *salt, size_t saltlen, size_t iter, size_t outlen, uint8_t *out);
functions.description: Derives a key from a password using PBKDF2 with HMAC-SM3. Callers provide the password bytes, a salt, an iteration count, and an output buffer of the desired length. Intended for generating cryptographic keys from passwords with the SM3 hash. Return value semantics are not documented here; consult the library for exact success/failure indicators.
requirements: pass must point to at least passlen bytes; the pointer must be valid for reading passlen bytes.
salt must point to at least saltlen bytes; the pointer must be valid for reading saltlen bytes.
saltlen should not exceed PBKDF2_MAX_SALT_SIZE (64), inferred from the defined constant.
iter should be within [PBKDF2_MIN_ITER, PBKDF2_MAX_ITER] (10000..INT_MAX), inferred from the defined constants.
out must point to a writable buffer of at least outlen bytes; the buffer will be filled with the derived key.
The function performs PBKDF2 key derivation using HMAC-SM3; outlen determines the length of the derived key to generate.

functions.name: pbkdf2_params_to_der
functions.signature: int pbkdf2_params_to_der(const uint8_t *salt, size_t saltlen, int iter, int keylen, int prf, uint8_t **out, size_t *outlen);
functions.description: Encode PBKDF2-params (RFC 2898/PKCS #5) into DER. This serializes salt, iterationCount, optional keyLength, and PRF into a DER SEQUENCE suitable for AlgorithmIdentifier parameters. In this implementation, prf must denote HMAC-SM3 (OID_hmac_sm3). Use when constructing PBKDF2 AlgorithmIdentifier parameters or embedding inside PBES2 parameters.
requirements: salt points to the salt buffer of length saltlen; if saltlen > 0, salt must be non-NULL.
iter must be a positive integer (PBKDF2 iterationCount INTEGER (1..MAX)).
keylen, if used, must be a positive integer (INTEGER (1..MAX)); whether 0/negative encodes omission is unknown.
prf must represent OID_hmac_sm3 per header comment.
out and outlen must be non-NULL and writable; out should reference a DER output buffer management scheme expected by the library (exact allocation/append semantics unknown).
Function return value semantics (success/failure codes) are unknown.

functions.name: pbkdf2_params_from_der
functions.signature: int pbkdf2_params_from_der(const uint8_t **salt, size_t *saltlen, int *iter, int *keylen, int *prf, const uint8_t **in, size_t *inlen);
functions.description: Decode a DER-encoded PBKDF2-params SEQUENCE, extracting salt, iterationCount, optional keyLength, and PRF. Use when parsing PBKDF2 parameters from an AlgorithmIdentifier or PBES2 structure.
requirements: in and inlen must point to a buffer containing a valid DER encoding of PBKDF2-params; inlen must reflect the remaining length.
salt and saltlen must be non-NULL; on success they will reference/describe the decoded salt inside the supplied DER buffer (lifetime tied to input buffer).
iter must be non-NULL to receive the iteration count; the decoded value must be >= 1.
keylen may be optional in DER; if present, keylen is set; if absent, behavior is unknown (e.g., set to 0 or left unchanged).
prf must be non-NULL; per header, only HMAC-SM3 (OID_hmac_sm3) is expected/accepted.
The function may advance *in and reduce *inlen; caller must provide mutable pointers. Exact advancement semantics are inferred from typical from_der patterns but not explicitly documented.
Function return value semantics (success/failure codes) are unknown.

functions.name: pbkdf2_params_print
functions.signature: int pbkdf2_params_print(FILE *fp, int fmt, int ind, const char *label, const uint8_t *d, size_t dlen);
functions.description: Pretty-print a DER-encoded PBKDF2-params structure to the given FILE stream for debugging or inspection. Provide formatting options via fmt/ind and an optional label.
requirements: fp must be a valid, writable FILE*.

functions.name: pbkdf2_algor_to_der
functions.signature: int pbkdf2_algor_to_der(const uint8_t *salt, size_t saltlen, int iter, int keylen, int prf, uint8_t **out, size_t *outlen);
functions.description: Encode an AlgorithmIdentifier for PBKDF2 into DER, including the PBKDF2-params sequence. Use when a full AlgorithmIdentifier object is required (e.g., in PBES2 keyDerivationFunc). PRF must be HMAC-SM3 per header note.
requirements: salt and saltlen specify the PBKDF2 salt; if saltlen > 0, salt must be non-NULL.

functions.name: pbkdf2_algor_from_der
functions.signature: int pbkdf2_algor_from_der(const uint8_t **salt, size_t *saltlen, int *iter, int *keylen, int *prf, const uint8_t **in, size_t *inlen);
functions.description: Decode an AlgorithmIdentifier containing PBKDF2 parameters from DER, extracting salt, iterationCount, optional keyLength, and PRF. Use for parsing keyDerivationFunc parameters in PBES2.
requirements: in and inlen must refer to a valid DER-encoded AlgorithmIdentifier with PBKDF2 parameters; pointers must be mutable so the function can advance them.
salt/saltlen, iter, keylen, and prf must be non-NULL to receive outputs; lifetimes of any returned pointers are tied to the input buffer.
The decoded PRF is expected to be HMAC-SM3 per header note.
Behavior when keyLength is absent is unknown (e.g., keylen may be set to 0 or left unchanged).
Function return value semantics are unknown.

functions.name: pbkdf2_algor_print
functions.signature: int pbkdf2_algor_print(FILE *fp, int fmt, int ind, const char *label, const uint8_t *d, size_t dlen);
functions.description: Pretty-print a DER-encoded AlgorithmIdentifier carrying PBKDF2 parameters to the given FILE stream with formatting controls. Useful for diagnostics.
requirements: fp must be valid and writable.
d must point to DER bytes of an AlgorithmIdentifier with PBKDF2 parameters; dlen supplies its length.

functions.name: x509_public_key_algor_to_der

On success, the function may advance *in and reduce *inlen by bytes consumed (inferred).

d must be non-NULL if dlen > 0.

functions.name: x509_exts_add_policy_mappings
functions.signature: int x509_exts_add_policy_mappings(uint8_t *exts, size_t *extslen, size_t maxlen, int critical, const uint8_t *d, size_t dlen);
functions.description: Appends a PolicyMappings extension using the provided DER-encoded PolicyMappings value. Returns 1 on success.
requirements: exts/extslen/maxlen buffer semantics apply; final size <= maxlen.
critical must be X509_non_critical or X509_critical (RFC suggests critical).
d must be DER-encoded PolicyMappings (SEQUENCE of PolicyMapping); dlen its length.
Non-NULL d when dlen > 0.

functions.name: x509_exts_add_subject_alt_name
functions.signature: int x509_exts_add_subject_alt_name(uint8_t *exts, size_t *extslen, size_t maxlen, int critical, const uint8_t *d, size_t dlen);
functions.description: Appends a SubjectAltName extension from a DER-encoded GeneralNames value. Returns 1 on success.
requirements: exts/extslen/maxlen must be valid; result length <= maxlen.
critical must be X509_non_critical or X509_critical (SAN is typically non-critical).
d must be DER-encoded GeneralNames; dlen its length.
d non-NULL if dlen > 0.

functions.name: x509_exts_add_issuer_alt_name
functions.signature: int x509_exts_add_issuer_alt_name(uint8_t *exts, size_t *extslen, size_t maxlen, int critical, const uint8_t *d, size_t dlen);
functions.description: Appends an IssuerAltName extension from a DER-encoded GeneralNames value. Returns 1 on success.
requirements: exts/extslen/maxlen valid; final size <= maxlen.
critical must be X509_non_critical or X509_critical (typically non-critical).
d must be DER-encoded GeneralNames; dlen its length.
d non-NULL if dlen > 0.

functions.name: x509_exts_add_subject_directory_attributes
functions.signature: int x509_exts_add_subject_directory_attributes(uint8_t *exts, size_t *extslen, size_t maxlen, int critical, const uint8_t *d, size_t dlen);
functions.description: Appends a SubjectDirectoryAttributes extension using a DER-encoded SEQUENCE OF Attribute. Returns 1 on success.
requirements: exts/extslen/maxlen valid; output length must not exceed maxlen.
critical must be X509_non_critical or X509_critical (MUST non-critical per comment).
d must be DER-encoded SEQUENCE OF Attribute; dlen length.
d non-NULL if dlen > 0.

functions.name: x509_exts_add_name_constraints
functions.description: Appends a NameConstraints extension composed from optional DER-encoded GeneralSubtrees for permitted and excluded sets. Returns 1 on success.
requirements: exts/extslen/maxlen must describe a valid buffer; final size <= maxlen.
critical must be X509_non_critical or X509_critical (usage typically critical for CAs).
permitted_subtrees and excluded_subtrees, when provided (len > 0), must be DER-encoded GeneralSubtrees SEQUENCE values.
Pointers with nonzero lengths must be non-NULL.

functions.name: x509_exts_add_policy_constraints
functions.signature:
int x509_exts_add_policy_constraints(uint8_t *exts, size_t *extslen, size_t maxlen, int critical,
	int require_explicit_policy, int inhibit_policy_mapping);
functions.description: Appends a PolicyConstraints extension built from the optional integer fields requireExplicitPolicy and inhibitPolicyMapping. Returns 1 on success.
requirements: exts/extslen/maxlen valid; final size <= maxlen.
critical must be X509_non_critical or X509_critical (MUST critical per comment).
require_explicit_policy and inhibit_policy_mapping are non-negative integers or a sentinel to omit (implementation-specific if 0 means present with value 0 or omitted; unknown).
exts and extslen must be non-NULL.

functions.name: x509_exts_add_basic_constraints
functions.signature: int x509_exts_add_basic_constraints(uint8_t *exts, size_t *extslen, size_t maxlen, int critical, int ca, int path_len_constraint);
functions.description: Appends a BasicConstraints extension indicating CA capability and optional pathLenConstraint. Returns 1 on success.
requirements: exts/extslen/maxlen valid; final size <= maxlen.
critical must be X509_non_critical or X509_critical (CA certs MUST critical; end-entity MAY).
ca is boolean-like (0 or nonzero).
path_len_constraint must be in range 0..X509_MAX_PATH_LEN_CONSTRAINT when present (per macro guidance); how absence is encoded is implementation-defined (unknown).

functions.name: x509_exts_add_ext_key_usage
functions.signature: int x509_exts_add_ext_key_usage(uint8_t *exts, size_t *extslen, size_t maxlen, int critical, const int *key_purposes, size_t key_purposes_cnt);
functions.description: Appends an Extended Key Usage extension from an array of KeyPurposeId OIDs (integers defined by library). Returns 1 on success.
requirements: exts/extslen/maxlen valid; final size <= maxlen.
critical must be X509_non_critical or X509_critical (MAY be either).
key_purposes points to an array of OID constants; key_purposes_cnt is number of elements and should be <= X509_MAX_KEY_PURPOSES.
key_purposes must be non-NULL when count > 0.

functions.name: x509_exts_add_crl_distribution_points_ex
functions.signature:
int x509_exts_add_crl_distribution_points_ex(uint8_t *exts, size_t *extslen, size_t maxlen, int critical, int oid,
	const char *http_uri, size_t http_urilen, const char *ldap_uri, size_t ldap_urilen);
functions.description: Appends a CRLDistributionPoints-like extension identified by oid, using provided HTTP and/or LDAP URIs to build DistributionPoints. Returns 1 on success.
requirements: exts/extslen/maxlen valid; final size <= maxlen.
critical must be X509_non_critical or X509_critical (per comment, CRLDP typically non-critical).
oid selects the extension OID (e.g., CRL DP or FreshestCRL); must be a supported OID by this API.
http_uri/ldap_uri may be NULL if corresponding length is 0; when length > 0 the pointer must be non-NULL and the string must have at least urilen bytes.
URIs must be valid IA5String content.

functions.name: x509_exts_add_crl_distribution_points
functions.signature:
int x509_exts_add_crl_distribution_points(uint8_t *exts, size_t *extslen, size_t maxlen, int critical,
	const char *http_uri, size_t http_urilen, const char *ldap_uri, size_t ldap_urilen);
functions.description: Appends a CRLDistributionPoints extension from provided HTTP/LDAP URIs. Convenience wrapper for the standard CRLDP OID. Returns 1 on success.
requirements: exts/extslen/maxlen valid; final size <= maxlen.
critical must be X509_non_critical or X509_critical.
http_uri/ldap_uri NULL only if length is 0; if length > 0 then pointer must be non-NULL and contain at least that many bytes.
URIs must be valid IA5String content.

functions.name: x509_exts_add_inhibit_any_policy
functions.signature: int x509_exts_add_inhibit_any_policy(uint8_t *exts, size_t *extslen, size_t maxlen, int critical, int skip_certs);
functions.description: Appends an InhibitAnyPolicy extension encoding SkipCerts as an INTEGER. Returns 1 on success.
requirements: exts/extslen/maxlen valid; final size <= maxlen.
critical must be X509_non_critical or X509_critical (MUST critical per comment).
skip_certs must be a non-negative integer.
exts and extslen must be non-NULL.

functions.name: x509_exts_add_freshest_crl
functions.signature: int x509_exts_add_freshest_crl(uint8_t *exts, size_t *extslen, size_t maxlen, int critical, const uint8_t *d, size_t dlen);
functions.description: Appends a FreshestCRL extension from a DER-encoded CRLDistributionPoints value. Returns 1 on success.
requirements: exts/extslen/maxlen valid; final size <= maxlen.
critical must be X509_non_critical or X509_critical (MUST non-critical per comment).
d must be DER-encoded CRLDistributionPoints; dlen its length.
d must be non-NULL when dlen > 0.

functions.name: x509_exts_add_authority_info_access
functions.description: Appends an AuthorityInfoAccess extension built from optional CA Issuers and OCSP URIs. Returns 1 on success.
requirements: exts/extslen/maxlen valid; final size <= maxlen.
critical must be X509_non_critical or X509_critical.
ca_issuers_uri (URI of a DER-encoded CA cert) and ocsp_uri may be NULL if corresponding length is 0; when length > 0 pointer must be non-NULL.
URIs must be valid IA5String content; lengths must match provided pointers.

functions.name: x509_exts_add_sequence
functions.signature:
int x509_exts_add_sequence(uint8_t *exts, size_t *extslen, size_t maxlen,
	int oid, int critical, const uint8_t *d, size_t dlen);
functions.description: Generic helper to append an extension identified by OID with the given criticality and DER-encoded value (OCTET STRING wrapped). Returns 1 on success.
requirements: exts/extslen/maxlen valid; final size <= maxlen.
oid must be a valid extension OID constant recognized by the library.
critical must be X509_non_critical or X509_critical.
d must be DER-encoded extension value (the inner ASN.1 value); dlen its length.
Non-NULL d if dlen > 0.

functions.name: x509_other_name_to_der
functions.description: Encodes OtherName ::= SEQUENCE { type-id OBJECT IDENTIFIER, value [0] EXPLICIT ANY } to DER. Returns 1 on success.
requirements: nodes/nodes_count describe the OID arcs for type-id; must be non-NULL with count > 0.
value/value_len are the DER encoding of the qualifier value for the given OID; may be empty only if schema allows (unknown).
out must point to a buffer pointer updated by the encoder (ASN.1 writer contract used in library); outlen updated with bytes written.
nodes_count must match actual nodes array length; value must be non-NULL when value_len > 0.

functions.name: x509_other_name_from_der
functions.description: Parses an OtherName structure from DER input, returning the OID nodes and the tagged value slice. Returns 1 on success.
requirements: in/inlen must point to DER buffer and remaining length; advanced on success.
nodes must have sufficient capacity for decoded arcs; nodes_count is input/output capacity/size (max capacity must be honored; exact behavior for overflow unknown).
On success, value points inside input to the EXPLICIT content and valuelen is its length; pointers remain valid while the backing buffer is valid.
All output pointers must be non-NULL.

functions.name: x509_other_name_print
functions.signature: int x509_other_name_print(FILE *fp, int fmt, int ind, const char *label, const uint8_t *d, size_t dlen);
functions.description: Pretty-prints a DER-encoded OtherName value to the given FILE with formatting options. Returns 1 on success.
requirements: fp must be a valid FILE* open for writing.
d must point to DER-encoded OtherName; dlen its length.
fmt/ind control formatting; accepted values are library-defined (unknown).
label may be NULL or a C-string; implementation prints accordingly.

functions.name: x509_edi_party_name_to_der
functions.signature:
int x509_edi_party_name_to_der(
	int assigner_tag, const uint8_t *assigner, size_t assigner_len,
	int party_name_tag, const uint8_t *party_name, size_t party_name_len,
	uint8_t **out, size_t *outlen);
functions.description: Encodes EDIPartyName ::= SEQUENCE { nameAssigner [0] EXPLICIT DirectoryString OPTIONAL, partyName [1] EXPLICIT DirectoryString } to DER. Returns 1 on success.
requirements: party_name_tag and party_name/party_name_len must specify a valid DirectoryString tag and bytes; required field.
assigner_tag/assigner/assigner_len are optional; when provided, tag must be a valid DirectoryString tag.
out/outlen must be valid pointers for writing DER.
When a length > 0 is provided, its pointer must be non-NULL.

functions.name: x509_edi_party_name_from_der
functions.signature:
int x509_edi_party_name_from_der(
	int *assigner_tag, const uint8_t **assigner, size_t *assigner_len,
	int *party_name_tag, const uint8_t **party_name, size_t *party_name_len,
	const uint8_t **in, size_t *inlen);
functions.description: Parses EDIPartyName from DER, returning optional nameAssigner and required partyName as DirectoryString-tagged values. Returns 1 on success.
requirements: in/inlen must reference a DER buffer; advanced on success.
Output pointers must be non-NULL and will reference slices of the input buffer.
If assigner is absent, assigner_tag may be set accordingly (implementation-specific sentinel).
Caller must ensure output storage for tags and lengths is valid.

functions.name: x509_edi_party_name_print
functions.signature: int x509_edi_party_name_print(FILE *fp, int fmt, int ind, const char *label, const uint8_t *d, size_t dlen);
functions.description: Pretty-prints a DER-encoded EDIPartyName to FILE with formatting options. Returns 1 on success.
requirements: fp valid for writing.
d points to DER-encoded EDIPartyName; dlen is its length.
fmt/ind control formatting; accepted values unspecified here.

functions.name: x509_general_name_to_der
functions.signature: int x509_general_name_to_der(int choice, const uint8_t *d, size_t dlen, uint8_t **out, size_t *outlen);
functions.description: Encodes GeneralName CHOICE with the provided choice tag and content bytes to DER. Returns 1 on success.

functions.name: x509_general_name_from_der
functions.signature: int x509_general_name_from_der(int *choice, const uint8_t **d, size_t *dlen, const uint8_t **in, size_t *inlen);
functions.description: Parses a GeneralName from DER input, returning the choice selector and a pointer/length to the content. Returns 1 on success.
requirements: in/inlen must point to DER buffer; advanced on success.
choice, d, dlen must be non-NULL; returned d points into input buffer.
Caller must interpret d based on choice (types vary by choice).

functions.name: x509_general_name_print
functions.signature: int x509_general_name_print(FILE *fp, int fmt, int ind, const char *label, int choice, const uint8_t *d, size_t dlen);
functions.description: Pretty-prints a GeneralName value according to the choice to the given FILE. Returns 1 on success.
requirements: fp valid for writing.
choice must correspond to the provided data d/dlen.
d must be the encoded content appropriate for choice (not necessarily full DER for IMPLICIT choices).
fmt/ind control formatting; details unspecified.

functions.name: x509_general_names_add_general_name
functions.signature:
int x509_general_names_add_general_name(uint8_t *gns, size_t *gnslen, size_t maxlen,
	int choice, const uint8_t *d, size_t dlen);
functions.description: Appends a GeneralName to a SEQUENCE OF GeneralName buffer. Returns 1 on success.

d/dlen must be valid content for the chosen type.

functions.name: x509_general_names_print
functions.signature: int x509_general_names_print(FILE *fp, int fmt, int ind, const char *label, const uint8_t *d, size_t dlen);
functions.description: Pretty-prints a DER-encoded GeneralNames (SEQUENCE OF GeneralName). Returns 1 on success.

d is DER-encoded GeneralNames; dlen length.
fmt/ind control formatting; specifics unspecified.

functions.name: x509_general_names_add_other_name
functions.description: Convenience to append an otherName entry to a GeneralNames buffer from OID nodes and a DER-encoded value. Returns 1 on success.
requirements: gns/gnslen/maxlen valid buffer; final size <= maxlen.
nodes/nodes_count describe a valid OBJECT IDENTIFIER; must be non-NULL with count > 0.
value/value_len are the DER content for the OtherName value; value non-NULL if value_len > 0.

functions.name: x509_general_names_add_edi_party_name
functions.description: Convenience to append an ediPartyName to a GeneralNames buffer using DirectoryString-tagged assigner (optional) and partyName (required). Returns 1 on success.
requirements: gns/gnslen/maxlen valid; final length <= maxlen.
party_name_tag/party_name/party_name_len must specify a valid DirectoryString; required.
assigner_tag/assigner/assigner_len optional but if provided must form a valid DirectoryString.

functions.name: x509_general_names_add_registered_id
functions.signature:
int x509_general_names_add_registered_id(uint8_t *gns, size_t *gnslen, size_t maxlen,
	const uint32_t *nodes, size_t nodes_cnt);
functions.description: Appends a registeredID GeneralName from an OBJECT IDENTIFIER given as nodes. Returns 1 on success.
requirements: gns/gnslen/maxlen valid; final length <= maxlen.
nodes must be non-NULL with nodes_cnt > 0 describing a valid OID.

functions.name: x509_uri_as_general_names_to_der_ex
functions.signature: int x509_uri_as_general_names_to_der_ex(int tag, const char *uri, size_t urilen, uint8_t **out, size_t *outlen);

tag must be a valid ASN.1 tag for the outer container (e.g., ASN1_TAG_SEQUENCE).
out/outlen must be valid for DER writing.

functions.name: x509_authority_key_identifier_to_der
functions.description: Encodes AuthorityKeyIdentifier SEQUENCE from optional keyIdentifier (OCTET STRING), authorityCertIssuer (GeneralNames), and authorityCertSerialNumber (INTEGER). Returns 1 on success.
requirements: Provide any subset of fields; pointers with nonzero length must be non-NULL.
issuer must be DER-encoded GeneralNames if provided; serial must be DER-encoded INTEGER; keyid is raw bytes for OCTET STRING content.
out/outlen must be valid for DER writing.

functions.name: x509_authority_key_identifier_from_der
functions.description: Parses AuthorityKeyIdentifier from DER input, returning slices for the optional fields. Returns 1 on success.
requirements: in/inlen must point to DER buffer; advanced on success.
Output pointers (keyid, issuer, serial) and their length outputs must be non-NULL; returned pointers reference input buffer memory.
Absent fields will likely yield length 0 and NULL pointer (implementation-specific).

functions.name: x509_authority_key_identifier_print
functions.signature: int x509_authority_key_identifier_print(FILE *fp, int fmt, int ind, const char *label, const uint8_t *d, size_t dlen);
functions.description: Pretty-prints a DER-encoded AuthorityKeyIdentifier value to FILE. Returns 1 on success.
requirements: fp valid for writing.
d points to DER-encoded AuthorityKeyIdentifier; dlen its length.
fmt/ind control formatting; specifics unspecified.

functions.name: x509_key_usage_name
functions.signature: const char *x509_key_usage_name(int flag);
functions.description: Returns the canonical name string for a single KeyUsage bit flag value (X509_KU_*).
requirements: flag should be a single defined bit (not a combination) from X509_KU_*.
Returns NULL or an implementation-defined string for unknown flags (behavior unknown).

functions.name: x509_key_usage_from_name
functions.signature: int x509_key_usage_from_name(int *flag, const char *name);
functions.description: Resolves a KeyUsage flag bit from its name string. Returns 1 on success, 0/negative on error.

functions.name: x509_key_usage_check

requirements: bits is a combination of X509_KU_* flags.
cert_type must be a library-defined certificate type constant (not provided here; unknown).

functions.name: x509_key_usage_print
functions.signature: int x509_key_usage_print(FILE *fp, int fmt, int ind, const char *label, int bits);
functions.description: Prints a human-readable representation of KeyUsage bits to FILE. Returns 1 on success.
requirements: fp valid for writing.
bits is a combination of X509_KU_* flags.
fmt/ind control formatting; unspecified.

functions.name: x509_display_text_check
functions.signature: int x509_display_text_check(int tag, const uint8_t *d, size_t dlen);
functions.description: Validates that the provided bytes conform to a permitted DisplayText CHOICE and length constraints (1..200). Returns 1 if valid.
requirements: tag must be a valid DisplayText tag (IA5String, VisibleString, BMPString, UTF8String).
d must be non-NULL when dlen > 0; dlen must be within [X509_DISPLAY_TEXT_MIN_LEN, X509_DISPLAY_TEXT_MAX_LEN].

functions.name: x509_display_text_to_der
functions.signature: int x509_display_text_to_der(int tag, const uint8_t *d, size_t dlen, uint8_t **out, size_t *outlen);

functions.name: x509_display_text_from_der
functions.signature: int x509_display_text_from_der(int *tag, const uint8_t **d, size_t *dlen, const uint8_t **in, size_t *inlen);
functions.description: Parses a DisplayText from DER, returning the tag and content slice. Returns 1 on success.
requirements: in/inlen must point to DER buffer; advanced on success.
tag, d, dlen must be non-NULL; returned d points into input buffer.
Caller must ensure DisplayText size and charset constraints as needed (or rely on parser).

functions.name: x509_display_text_print
functions.signature: int x509_display_text_print(FILE *fp, int fmt, int ind, const char *label, int tag, const uint8_t *d, size_t dlen);
functions.description: Prints a DisplayText value to FILE according to its tag. Returns 1 on success.
requirements: fp valid for writing.
tag must match the provided content d/dlen.
d points to the string content bytes, not including tag/length (per typical print helpers).

functions.name: x509_notice_reference_to_der
functions.description: Encodes NoticeReference ::= SEQUENCE { organization DisplayText, noticeNumbers SEQUENCE OF INTEGER } to DER. Returns 1 on success.

notice_numbers points to an array of INTEGERs; count must be <= X509_MAX_NOTICE_NUMBERS.
out/outlen valid for writing.
Pointers must be non-NULL when lengths/counts > 0.

functions.name: x509_notice_reference_from_der
functions.signature:
int x509_notice_reference_from_der(

functions.name: x509_notice_reference_print

functions.description: Prints a DER-encoded NoticeReference. Returns 1 on success.
requirements: fp valid for writing.
d points to DER NoticeReference; dlen its length.

functions.name: x509_user_notice_to_der
functions.description: Encodes UserNotice ::= SEQUENCE { noticeRef NoticeReference OPTIONAL, explicitText DisplayText OPTIONAL } to DER. Returns 1 on success.

out/outlen valid for writing.
At least one of noticeRef or explicitText may be present; both may be omitted (schema allows OPTIONAL for both).

functions.name: x509_user_notice_from_der
functions.signature:
int x509_user_notice_from_der(
	int *notice_ref_org_tag, const uint8_t **notice_ref_org, size_t *notice_ref_org_len,

functions.description: Parses UserNotice from DER, returning optional NoticeReference and explicitText if present. Returns 1 on success.

notice_ref_notice_numbers must have capacity for up to max_notice_ref_notice_numbers; count output will be <= max.
All output pointers provided must be valid and will reference data within input buffer.

functions.name: x509_user_notice_print
functions.signature: int x509_user_notice_print(FILE *fp, int fmt, int ind, const char *label, const uint8_t *d, size_t dlen);
functions.description: Prints a DER-encoded UserNotice value to FILE. Returns 1 on success.

functions.description: Returns the name of a PolicyQualifierId OID (e.g., id-qt-cps, id-qt-unotice) for a given library OID constant.

functions.name: x509_qualifier_id_from_name

functions.name: x509_qualifier_id_from_der
functions.signature: int x509_qualifier_id_from_der(int *oid, const uint8_t **in, size_t *inlen);
functions.description: Parses a PolicyQualifierId OBJECT IDENTIFIER from DER input. Returns 1 on success.

oid must be non-NULL to receive decoded OID constant.

functions.name: x509_qualifier_id_to_der
functions.signature: int x509_qualifier_id_to_der(int oid, uint8_t **out, size_t *outlen);
functions.description: Encodes a PolicyQualifierId OBJECT IDENTIFIER to DER. Returns 1 on success.
requirements: oid must be a recognized PolicyQualifierId constant.
